› Microcontroller Abstraction (MCAL)

AUTOSAR Classic Microcontroller Abstraction (MCAL)

a Microcontroller abstração camada (MCAL) contém hardware-spezifische controlador para interna Mikrocontroller-Peripherie (ADC-Wandler, PWM-Generatoren, hardware-Watchdog) e entkoppelt obere BSW-Schichten da Silizium-plataforma.

GERADO POR IA não revisado Modelo: claude-opus-5-5 · Effort: high · Temperatura: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7985d6716d3c Procedência
Âncora causal: R20-11 Válido a partir de R20-11 Sintetizado para esta versão de especificação.

Arquitetura do sistema & papel do cluster de módulos

O cluster “Microcontroller Abstraction” forma a camada de software mais baixa da Classic Platform. As especificações dos drivers ADC e PWM registram expressamente que esses módulos residem no nível de arquitetura mais baixo e, por isso, não oferecem callbacks para camadas inferiores (SWS ADC p. 79, SWS PWM p. 40). Seus usuários são módulos da abstração de ECU e dos serviços de sistema, principalmente IoHwAb, WdgIf/WdgM, bem como EcuM e BswM. Normativos para a R20-11 são os Requirements do payload. Passagens de documentos de releases posteriores servem aqui apenas para fins ilustrativos, como o exemplo de ADC da IoHwAb (IoHwAb p. 55).

  • O Adc converte canais analógicos em grupos. Uma conversão é disparada por software ou hardware ([SWS_Adc_00514]). Os resultados ficam em buffers fornecidos pelo usuário ([SWS_Adc_91000]).
  • O Pwm gera sinais modulados por largura de pulso com período e duty cycle ([SWS_Pwm_91001]). Opcionalmente, ele reporta bordas de sinal ([SWS_Pwm_00109]).
  • O Wdg opera o watchdog de hardware interno ou externo por meio de uma condição de disparo ([SWS_Wdg_00144]).
  • O Spi e o Dio estão comprovados no payload como vias de acesso de um watchdog externo ([SWS_Wdg_00076]). O payload não contém Requirements de SWS próprios desses dois módulos.
  • O Port está comprovado via Port_Init como “Initializes the Port Driver module” na lista de interfaces do EcuM (SWS EcuM p. 142). Um diagrama localiza a “Port Logic” entre a unidade PWM e o pino (RS PWM p. 14).

Diagrama de contexto: Os drivers MCAL são inicializados por EcuM/BswM, utilizados por IoHwAb e WdgIf, e reportam erros ao DET/DEM; um watchdog externo acessa o hardware via Spi ou Dio. Fontes: [SWS_Wdg_00076], [SWS_Adc_00082], [SWS_Pwm_00198], [SWS_Wdg_00111], [SWS_Adc_00377], [SWS_Pwm_00104], Modemanagement p. 54

Interação & caminhos de interação

Caminho de dados do ADC. O fluxo começa com o buffer de resultados.

  1. Após cada reset e antes da primeira conversão de grupo, o usuário deve definir o buffer de resultados do grupo com Adc_SetupResultBuffer ([SWS_Adc_91000], SWS ADC p. 54).
  2. Adc_StartGroupConversion redefine o ponteiro interno do buffer. A notificação não é ativada automaticamente com isso ([SWS_Adc_00367], SWS ADC p. 57).
  3. Após cada conversão de grupo concluída, o driver chama IoHwAb_AdcNotification<#groupID> ([SWS_Adc_00082]).
  4. O usuário lê os resultados por uma de duas vias:
    • Adc_ReadGroup copia-os ([SWS_Adc_00369]).
    • Adc_GetStreamLastPointer fornece um ponteiro para o buffer ([SWS_Adc_00375]).

Quantos resultados o buffer comporta depende do modo de acesso: Single ou Streaming ([SWS_Adc_00528]). No modo Streaming, o buffer é organizado de forma linear ou circular ([SWS_Adc_00519]).

Diagrama de sequência: Conversão contínua disparada por software com notificação – configurar buffer, ativar notificação, iniciar, notificar e ler a cada rodada, parar. Fontes: SWS ADC p. 92, [SWS_Adc_91000], [SWS_Adc_00082], SWS ADC p. 70

Caminho de controle de PWM. O usuário ajusta o sinal por meio de dois serviços:

  • Pwm_SetDutyCycle altera apenas o duty cycle ([SWS_Pwm_91000]).
  • Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty altera o período e o duty cycle ([SWS_Pwm_91001]). O período só pode ser alterado em canais da classe PWM_VARIABLE_PERIOD ([SWS_Pwm_00110]); caso contrário, o driver reporta PWM_E_PERIOD_UNCHANGEABLE ([SWS_Pwm_40002]).

Notificações de borda chegam ao usuário por meio de Pwm_Notification_<#Channel>. O determinante é a última chamada de Pwm_EnableNotification ou Pwm_DisableNotification ([SWS_Pwm_00105], [SWS_Pwm_91004]). Pwm_GetOutputState lê o estado interno do sinal de saída ([SWS_Pwm_00100]). De acordo com o diagrama, essa é a tomada de sinal antes da lógica de porta, não o nível no pino (RS PWM p. 14).

Caminho do watchdog. A cadeia de chamadas percorre três níveis:

  • O WdgM controla o driver por meio de WdgIf_SetMode e WdgIf_SetTriggerCondition (SWS WdgM p. 86).
  • O WdgIf mapeia esses serviços para a respectiva instância do driver por meio de DeviceIndex (SWS WdgIf p. 17).
  • O Wdg converte o timeout de milissegundos em um valor de contador, levando em consideração o modo atual ([SWS_Wdg_00138], [SWS_Wdg_00139]).

Watchdogs internos e externos diferem apenas no acesso ao hardware:

  • Um driver interno acessa diretamente o hardware ([SWS_Wdg_00161]).
  • Um driver externo utiliza Spi ou Dio e mantém os parâmetros necessários para isso em sua configuração ([SWS_Wdg_00076], [SWS_Wdg_00078]).
  • As APIs de ambas as variantes são semanticamente idênticas ([SWS_Wdg_00077]).
  • Se houver várias instâncias, os nomes das APIs são expandidos ([SWS_Wdg_00172]).

Diagrama de sequência: A definição da condição de disparo é desacoplada temporalmente da operação cíclica do hardware; com o contador em 0, o disparo não ocorre. Fontes: SWS Wdg p. 31, [SWS_Wdg_00134], [SWS_Wdg_00135], [SWS_Wdg_00136]

Sincronização, reentrância e contextos de tarefas

Os módulos diferem claramente em suas garantias de reentrância:

  • As APIs do caminho de dados do ADC são reentrantes.
  • Os serviços de PWM relacionados a canais são reentrantes apenas para canais distintos.
  • A inicialização, as APIs de power state e todos os serviços do Wdg não são reentrantes.
APISync/AsyncReentrânciaReferência
Adc_StartGroupConversionassíncronoreentrante[SWS_Adc_00367]
Adc_ReadGroupsíncronoreentrante[SWS_Adc_00369]
Adc_SetPowerStatesíncrononão reentrante[SWS_Adc_00475]
Pwm_SetDutyCycleassíncronoreentrante para canais diferentes[SWS_Pwm_91000]
Pwm_Initsíncrononão reentrante[SWS_Pwm_00095]
Wdg_SetMode / Wdg_SetTriggerConditionsíncrononão reentrante[SWS_Wdg_00107], [SWS_Wdg_00155]

Para a consistência de dados, o Wdg define áreas exclusivas por meio do BSW Scheduler. Como módulo MCAL, o driver interno também pode desabilitar interrupções diretamente ([SWS_Wdg_00040]). Durante a troca de modo e a rotina de operação, o estado WDG_BUSY indica acessos concorrentes ([SWS_Wdg_00018], [SWS_Wdg_00052]).

Funções agendadas. Adc_Main_PowerTransitionManager e Pwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager são executadas ciclicamente via SchM ([SWS_Adc_00479], [SWS_Pwm_00189]). A sua taxa é variável, pois elas são necessárias apenas durante uma transição em andamento ([SWS_Adc_00500]). Antes da inicialização, elas retornam sem notificação do DET ([SWS_Adc_00502]).

Contexto de interrupção. É provável que as notificações de grupo e de borda sejam executadas no contexto de interrupção. Dois fatores apontam para isso: o driver PWM redefine a flag de interrupção pertencente à notificação (SWS PWM p. 42). Além disso, o exemplo do MemMap inclui uma BswInterruptEntity Adc_IsrGroupScanCompleted (SWS MemMap p. 54). Portanto, os callbacks devem permanecer curtos. A reentrância de Pwm_Notification_<#Channel> depende expressamente da implementação do usuário ([SWS_Pwm_00105]).

Sistemas multinúcleo. O Adc e o Pwm devem rejeitar mapeamentos de partições que a implementação não suporte ([SWS_Adc_00531], [SWS_Pwm_00203]). As partições de kernel do ADC são um subconjunto das partições de usuário ([SWS_Adc_CONSTR_00001]). A isso se adequa o padrão Master-Satellite com divisão em kernel e parte de interface (BSW Distribution p. 18).

Ciclos de vida e modos operacionais

Inicialização. O EcuM chama Adc_Init ([SWS_Adc_00365], SWS ADC p. 91). A descrição da estrutura do EcuM menciona adicionalmente Port_Init, Pwm_Init, Spi_Init e Wdg_Init (SWS EcuM p. 34). Uma variante controlada pelo BswM inicializa na ordem Port, Dio, Adc, Spi (Modemanagement p. 54). Interpretação: o Port provavelmente fica no início porque a configuração dos pinos é pré-requisito para os demais drivers de periféricos.

ADC. O driver transiciona com Adc_Init de ADC_UNINIT para ADC_INIT e retorna com Adc_DeInit (SWS ADC p. 31). Cada grupo passa pelos estados ADC_IDLE, ADC_BUSY, ADC_COMPLETED e ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED ([SWS_Adc_00513]). O modo Continuous está disponível apenas com trigger de software ([SWS_Adc_00515]). Adc_DeInit coloca o hardware em um estado semelhante a um reset ([SWS_Adc_00366]). Ele só pode ser chamado quando todos os grupos estiverem em ADC_IDLE (SWS ADC p. 59).

PWM. Após Pwm_Init, as saídas são Low, High ou moduladas, conforme a configuração. As notificações permanecem desativadas até que Pwm_EnableNotification seja chamado ([SWS_Pwm_00095], SWS PWM p. 46). Pwm_DeInit define as saídas para o estado de Idle e desabilita as interrupções ([SWS_Pwm_00096], SWS PWM p. 27).

Watchdog. Wdg_Init define o modo padrão e o timeout inicial ([SWS_Wdg_00001], [SWS_Wdg_00100]). Depois disso, os modos WDGIF_OFF_MODE, WDGIF_SLOW_MODE e WDGIF_FAST_MODE podem ser selecionados ([SWS_Wdg_00160]). Não existe função de DeInit. A desativação é feita, se permitida, por meio do modo OFF ([SWS_Wdg_00031]).

Power states de Adc e Pwm. A transição ocorre em duas etapas:

  1. *_PreparePowerState inicia-a ([SWS_Adc_00478], [SWS_Pwm_00183]).
  2. No caso assíncrono, a função principal conclui-a e reporta prontidão por meio de IoHwAb_*_NotifyReadyForPowerState<#Mode> ([SWS_Adc_00480], [SWS_Pwm_00198]).
  3. *_SetPowerState realiza a troca ([SWS_Adc_00475], [SWS_Pwm_00166]).

Previamente, os SWCs responsáveis, como a IoHwAb, devem definir os canais para Idle e cancelar o registro das notificações (SWS PWM p. 36). Na própria transição, são permitidas apenas reconfigurações específicas da transição ([SWS_Adc_00484]).

Diagrama de sequência: Após uma troca de modo do BswM, a IoHwAb coordena a comutação de power state em duas etapas de Adc e Pwm, assincronamente com callbacks de prontidão ou sincronamente via consulta. Fontes: IoHwAb p. 57, IoHwAb p. 58, [SWS_Adc_00501], [SWS_Pwm_00190]

Tratamento de erros, rastreamento pelo DET e degradação

Erros de desenvolvimento (DET). Todos os três drivers especificados os reportam por meio de Det_ReportError ([SWS_Adc_00377], [SWS_Pwm_00104], [SWS_Wdg_00111]):

  • O Adc, entre outros, ADC_E_UNINIT e ADC_E_PARAM_GROUP ([SWS_Adc_91005]).
  • O Pwm, PWM_E_UNINIT e PWM_E_PARAM_CHANNEL ([SWS_Pwm_20002], [SWS_Pwm_30002]).
  • O Wdg, em caso de estado incorreto, WDG_E_DRIVER_STATE ([SWS_Wdg_00017], [SWS_Wdg_00035]).

Erros em tempo de execução. Aqui existem vários casos:

  • O ADC reporta ADC_E_BUSY, entre outros casos, quando uma conversão sem queuing já estiver em andamento ([SWS_Adc_91006], SWS ADC p. 95).
  • Se ainda houver canais ativos durante a troca de power state, ambos os drivers reportam *_E_NOT_DISENGAGED ([SWS_Adc_00487], [SWS_Pwm_00202]).
  • O ADC classifica um estado de potência de destino inalcançável no R20-11 como erro de tempo de execução ([SWS_Adc_00489]), ao passo que o PWM o classifica como erro do DET ([SWS_Pwm_00175]).

Erros de produção (DEM). Estes estão especificados no payload apenas para o Wdg e são reportados através de Dem_SetEventStatus ([SWS_Wdg_00111]):

  • WDG_E_MODE_FAILED em caso de falha na mudança de modo; Wdg_SetMode retorna então E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Wdg_00016], [SWS_Wdg_00180]).
  • WDG_E_DISABLE_REJECTED, quando a desativação não é permitida ([SWS_Wdg_00025], [SWS_Wdg_00182]).

Degradação e estados seguros.

  • Pwm_SetOutputToIdle define imediatamente a saída para o estado de repouso configurado ([SWS_Pwm_91002], SWS PWM p. 31).
  • Pwm_GetOutputState retorna defensivamente PWM_LOW antes da inicialização ou em caso de canal inválido ([SWS_Pwm_30051]).
  • No watchdog, o reset é o último nível de contingência. Um timeout de 0 aciona um reset da ECU quase imediato ([SWS_Wdg_00140]). Um contador de trigger expirado faz o watchdog expirar ([SWS_Wdg_00135]).
  • O driver rejeita timeouts excessivamente grandes com WDG_E_PARAM_TIMEOUT ([SWS_Wdg_00146]).
  • No ADC, mecanismos de prioridade com Abort/Restart ou Suspend/Resume controlam como grupos preempcionados são retomados ([SWS_Adc_00522], [SWS_Adc_00523]). A verificação de limites filtra resultados fora da faixa selecionada ([SWS_Adc_00524]).

Guia de cluster gerado por IA com base nos requisitos e passagens de documentos da R20-11 contidos no payload; por falta de requisitos próprios no payload, Dio, Port e Spi são descritos apenas por meio de suas interfaces com os demais módulos. Vinculativos são os elementos de especificação com link.

Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

## Implementer's Guides

Dieser Abschnitt gilt nur für Implementer's Guides (Rezepte `element-impl@1`,
`module-impl-guide@1`, `cluster-impl-guide@1`). Die Rezepte der User Guides
betten die Richtlinien ohne diesen Abschnitt ein; seine Änderung lässt deren
Prompt-Hashes unberührt.

- Frage: Was muss eine korrekte Implementierung leisten? Nicht: Wie benutze ich das?
- Das Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai impl-guide">` und endet mit genau
  einem `<p class="ai-note">`. Erlaubte Elemente wie oben.
- Pflichtgliederung als `<h4>` in dieser Reihenfolge, jede Überschrift genau
  einmal: „Verpflichtungen“, „Vorbedingungen und Zustände“, „Fehlerbehandlung“,
  „Aufrufkontext und Nebenläufigkeit“, „Wechselwirkungen“, „Prüfkriterien“,
  „Annahmen“. Ein Abschnitt ohne Beleg im Payload enthält nur den Satz
  „Die Quellen enthalten dazu keine Aussage.“
- Verpflichtungen: jede einschlägige Requirement-ID aus dem Payload als Liste
  mit `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">`.
- Prüfkriterien: eine nummerierte Liste `<ol class="impl-checks">`; jeder
  Eintrag ist eine testbare Aussage und trägt die belegende Requirement-ID als
  `<li data-sws="SWS_…">`. Nur IDs aus dem Payload.
- Annahmen (Annahmenpflicht): jede Annahme steht im Abschnitt „Annahmen“ als
  Listeneintrag mit Begründung und zusätzlich im Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: … -->`. Ohne Annahmen steht dort „Keine Annahmen.“.
  Angaben, die nicht aus dem Payload stammen (z. B. eine Dateistruktur nach
  AUTOSAR-Konvention), sind immer Annahmen und zählen zum Annahmenbudget.

KONTEXT-SYNTHESE- & EVIDENZ-REGELN (CONCEPT-0056):
1. KONTINUIERLICHE SYNTHESE: Alle übergebenen Inbound-Snippets fließen ohne Kurationspause ein.
2. ZWEISTUFIGE EVIDENZ-KENNZEICHNUNG:
   - VERIFIED (Score >= 0.95): Normativ verbindliche Belege, faktischer Text, Badge <span class="badge-pill bp-curated">🔒 Verifizierter Kontext</span>.
   - UNVERIFIED (0.70 <= Score < 0.95): Zwingend mit folgender Warnbox formatieren:
     <div class="ai-unverified-evidence" data-snippet-id="{ID}" data-confidence="{SCORE}">
       <div class="ai-unverified-header">
         <span class="badge-pill bp-ai">⚠️ UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS &bull; Konfidenz: {SCORE}</span>
         <span class="ai-unverified-actions">
           <a href="spec/record.html?id={REC_ID}#curate-{ID}" class="btn-curate-inline dossier-open-link" data-dossier-target="dossier-modal-{REC_ID}" data-snippet-id="{ID}">🔍 Im Curation-Editor prüfen &rarr;</a>
         </span>
       </div>
       <p class="ai-unverified-body">
         <strong>UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS (Nicht ohne formale Kuration für Serienentwicklung verwenden):</strong><br>
         <em>Interpretation / Vorläufiger Kontext:</em> [Interpretation der Anforderung]
       </p>
     </div>
3. DUKTUS FÜR UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESEN: Als abgeleitete Vermutung formulieren ('dürfte', 'lässt sich ableiten', 'Interpretation:'), niemals als verbindlicher Normentext.
4. TOKEN-BUDGET: Bis zu 90% des Kontextfensters können genutzt werden. Output ist limitiert auf max 8192 Tokens.
5. TRIVIALITÄTS-FILTER (INV-TRIVIALITY-WHITELIST-04): Enums, Typen und Methoden mit State-Machine-, Lifecycle-, E2E- oder Concurrency-Bezug sind niemals trivial.

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_2_3_1_3_Documentation_Support",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "TPS_ECUConfiguration",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "2.3.1.3 Documentation Support\nAUTOSAR provides support for integrated and well-structured documentation. More\ndetails about the AUTOSAR Documentation Support concept can be found in the\nAUTOSAR Generic Structure Template [4].\nThe documentation can be specified within in the following levels:\n• a single paragraph can be inserted in any Identifiable element using the\ndesc element.\n• a documentation block is available in any Identifiable element as intro-\nduction. This type of documentation is typically used to capture a short intro-\nduction about the role of an element or respectively how it is built.\n• a standalone documentation structured into multiple chapters is also offered in\nAUTOSAR. It is provided as Documentation which is an ARElement of its own\nrights allowing for a reference to the documents context.\nWith the introduction of this concept the container and parameter notes in the ECU\nConfiguration Parameter Definition XML file are split into a desc and an introduc-\ntion field. The desc field contains a brief description about the element and the\nintroduction field contains the documentation about how the element is built and\nused.\nIn the ECU Configuration Parameter Definition XML file of the current AUTOSAR Re-\nlease the proper usage of the desc and the introduction fields is not guaranteed.\nTherefore the content of the desc and introduction shall be read as one cohesive\nnote.\nListing 2.4 shows the split of the desc and introduction.\n<ECUC-MODULE-DEF>\n<SHORT-NAME>Adc</SHORT-NAME>\n<CONTAINERS>\n<ECUC-PARAM-CONF-CONTAINER-DEF>\n<SHORT-NAME>AdcHwUnit</SHORT-NAME>\n<DESC>\n<L-2 L=\"EN\">This container contains the Driver configuration (\nparameters) depending on grouping of channels</L-2>\n</DESC>\n<INTRODUCTION>\n<P>\n<L-1 L=\"EN\">This container could contain HW specific parameters\nwhich are not defined in the Standardized Module Definition.\nThey shall be added in the Vendor Specific Module Definition.<\n/L-1>\n</P>\n</INTRODUCTION>\n<LOWER-MULTIPLICITY>1</LOWER-MULTIPLICITY>\n<UPPER-MULTIPLICITY-INFINITE>true</UPPER-MULTIPLICITY-INFINITE>\n</ECUC-PARAM-CONF-CONTAINER-DEF>\n</CONTAINERS>\n</ECUC-MODULE-DEF>\nListing 2.4: Example for desc and introduction\nListing 2.5 shows the usage of the Documentation element to describe elements like\nchapters, lists, tables and figures. For details on this description means please refer to\nthe AUTOSAR Generic Structure Template [4].\n<DOCUMENTATION>\n<SHORT-NAME>Adc_AddInfo</SHORT-NAME>\n<CONTEXTS>\n<DOCUMENTATION-CONTEXT>\n<SHORT-NAME>AUTOSAR_Adc</SHORT-NAME>\n<IDENTIFIABLE-REF DEST=\"ECUC-MODULE-DEF\">/AUTOSAR/Adc</IDENTIFIABLE-\nREF>\n</DOCUMENTATION-CONTEXT>\n</CONTEXTS>\n<DOCUMENTATION-CONTENT>\n<CHAPTER>\n<SHORT-NAME>Introduction</SHORT-NAME>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">The ADC module initializes and controls the internal\nAnalogue Digital Converter Unit(s) of the microcontroller. It\nprovides services to start and stop a conversion respectively to\nenable and disable the trigger source for a conversion.</L-1></P>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">The consistency of the group channel results can be\nobtained with the following methods on the application side:</L-1>\n</P>\n<LIST>\n<ITEM>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">Using group notification mechanism</L-1></P>\n</ITEM>\n<ITEM>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">Polling via API function Adc_GetGroupStatus</L-1><\n/P>\n</ITEM>\n</LIST>\n<TABLE>\n<TGROUP COLS=\"2\">\n<THEAD>\n<ROW>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">column1</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">column2</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n</ROW>\n</THEAD>\n<TBODY>\n<ROW>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">element11</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">element12</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n</ROW>\n<ROW>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">element21</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n<ENTRY>\n<P><L-1 L=\"EN\">element22</L-1></P>\n</ENTRY>\n</ROW>\n</TBODY>\n</TGROUP>\n</TABLE>\n</CHAPTER>\n</DOCUMENTATION-CONTENT>\n</DOCUMENTATION>\nListing 2.5: Documentation Example"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "4.3.3 Software Module Design Requirements\n[SRS_BSW_00007] All Basic SW Modules written in C language shall conform to\nthe MISRA C 2012 Standard. ⌈\nDescription:\nMISRA C (see [5]) describes programming rules for the C programming\nlanguage and a process to implement and follow these rules.\nOnly in technically reasonable, exceptional cases MISRA violations are\npermissible. Such violations against MISRA rules shall be clearly identified and\ndocumented within comments in the C source code (including rationale why\nMISRA rule is violated).\nExamples of MISRA rules violations shall look like:\n/* MR12 RULE XX VIOLATION: Reason */\n/* MR12 DIR XX VIOLATION: Reason */\nRationale:\nPortability, maintainability, error avoidance, safety\nUse Case:\nSoftware for safety relevant systems\nDependencies:\n–\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n[5]\n⌋(RS_BRF_01056)\n[SRS_BSW_00300] All AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules shall be identified by\nan unambiguous name ⌈\nDescription:\nAll AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules shall be identified by an unambiguous\nname. The module name is always part of related files.\nConvention for module related files:\n• <Module name>_*.*\n• Spelling of module name: First letter of each word upper case,\nconsecutive letters lower case\n• Module name: 2..8 letters, derived from [7]\n• Wildcard replacement according to module related file set (either basic\nand recommended)\nRationale:\nThe module name serves as an identifier and classification mechanism in order\nto group module related files.\nUse Case:\nExample: Eep.c, Eep.h\n▽\n△\nDependencies:\n–\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n[7]\n⌋(RS_BRF_01024)\n[SRS_BSW_00413] An index-based accessing of the instances of BSW modules\nshall be done ⌈\nDescription:\nIf instances of BSW modules are characterized by:\n• same vendor and\n• same functionality and\n• same hardware device\nthey shall be accessed index based.\nRationale:\n–\nUse Case:\n–\nDependencies:\n[SRS_BSW_00347] Naming separation of drivers\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n–\n⌋()\n[SRS_BSW_00347] A Naming seperation of different instances of BSW drivers\nshall be in place ⌈\nDescription:\nDriver modules shall be named according to the following rules (only for\nimplementation, not for the software specification):\n• First the module name has to be listed: <Module Abbreviation>\n• After that the vendor Id defined in the AUTOSAR vendor list has to be\ngiven <Vendor Id>\n• At last a vendor specific name (the vendor API infix) follows <Vendor API\ninfix>\n• Only for API names, last name shall be <API Service name>\n• All parts shall be separated by underscores \"_\".\n• This naming extension applies to the following externally visible\nelements of the module:\n– File names\n– API names\n– Published parameters\n– Memory allocation keyword\n• For API names, <Vendor specific name> should be followed by \"_\" and\nthen <API Service Name>.\n▽\n▽\n△\n△\n• For the creation of file names, no trailing underscore shall be added.\n• For Published parameters and Memory allocation keyword names,\n<Vendor Specific name> shall have a trailing underscores.\nRationale:\nAvoidance of name clashes\nUse Case:\nExamples:\n• EEPROM (LD): Eep_21_LDExtEepDriver.c\n• Published parameters: EEP_21_LDEXT_SW_MAJOR_VERSION\n• API: Eep_21_LDExt_Init\nDependencies:\n–\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n[7] List of Basic Software Modules (Module Abbreviations)\n⌋(RS_BRF_01024)\n[SRS_BSW_00441] Naming convention for type, macro and function ⌈\nDescription:\nAll AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules shall label enumeration literals and\n#defines according to the following scheme:\n• Composition: <Module Abbreviation>_<Specific name>\n• <Module Abbreviation> shall be written in UPPERCASE\n• <Specific name> shall be written in UPPERCASE\n• <Module Abbreviation> and <Specific name> shall be separated by\nunderscore\n• If <Specific name> consists of several words, they shall be separated by\nunderscore\nThe #define E_OK and E_NOT_OK are exceptions to this.\nRationale:\nEnhance readability and unique classification of enumeration literals and\n#defines identifiers.\nUse Case:\nExample #define:\n#define EEP_PARAM_CONFIG\n#define EEP_SIZE\nExample enumeration literals:\ntypedef enum\n{\nEEP_DRA_CONFIG = 0,\nEEP_ARE = 1,\nEEP_EV = 2\n} Eep_NotificationType;\nDependencies:\n[SRS_BSW_00331] [SRS_BSW_00327] [SRS_BSW_00335]\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n–\n⌋(RS_BRF_01024)\n[SRS_BSW_00305] Data types naming convention ⌈\nDescription:\nAll AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules shall label data types according to the\nfollowing scheme:\n• Composition of type: <Module name>_<Type name>Type\n• Only one underscore between module name and type name\n• < Type name > shall be written in UpperCamelCase.\nNote:\nBasic AUTOSAR types ([SRS_BSW_00304]) need not support the scheme\ndefined here.\nRationale:\nEnhance readability and unique classification of data type identifiers.\nDependencies:\n–\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n–\n⌋(RS_BRF_01024)\n[SRS_BSW_00307] Global variables naming convention ⌈\nDescription:\n• All AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules shall label global variables\naccording to the following scheme:\n• Composition of name: <Module name>_<Variable name>\n• Only one underscore between module name and variable name\n• Spelling of name: First letter of each word upper case, consecutive\nletters lower case\nRationale:\nEnhance readability and unique classification of global variables.\nUse Case:\n–\nDependencies:\n–\nSupporting\nMaterial:\n–\n⌋(RS_BRF_01024)"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_1_3_1_Example_Configuration",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_ADCDriver",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.3.1 Example: Configuration\nThe example configuration consists of three ADC groups. Group 1 consists of 2 chan-\nnels, group 2 and group 3 consist of one channel each. For group 1 and 2 the group\naccess mode ADC_ACCESS_MODE_STREAMING is configured. The group access\nmode of group 3 is ADC_ACCESS_MODE_SINGLE. The ADC driver will store the con-\nversion results of group 1-3 in three application buffers, accessed with three configured\nADC_RESULT_POINTER :\nG1_ResultPtr, G2_ResultPtr and G3_ResultPtr."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_1_3_3_Example_Adc_GetStreamLastPointer_Usage",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_ADCDriver",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.1.3.3 Example: Adc_GetStreamLastPointer Usage\nThe ADC driver stores the conversion results of group G1, G2 and G3 in the according\nresult buffer G1_ResultBuffer[], G2_ResultBuffer[] and G3_ResultBuffer[]. A direct ac-\ncess from the ADC API functions to the ADC hardware result register is not supported\nfrom the ADC driver.\nThe user provides three pointers G1_SamplePtr, G2_SamplePtr and G3_SamplePtr\nwhich will point to the ADC application result buffer after calling Adc_GetStream\nLastPointer.Precisely pointer G1_SamplePtr points, after calling Adc_GetStreamLast\nPointer, to the latest G1_CH0 result of the latest completed conversion round (G1_CH0\nis the first channel in G1 group definition).The application result buffer layout is shown\nin Figure 2. The application result buffer of group 1 holds three times the streaming\nresults of G1_CH0 and then three times the streaming results of G1_CH1. Knowing\nthe application result buffer layout, the user is able to access all group channel results\nof the latest conversion round. G2_SamplePtr and G3_SamplePtr are also aligned,\nafter calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer, to point to the latest result of the first group\nchannel of the according group. Both groups have only one channel. G2_SamplePtr\npoints to one of the G2_CH2 results (the latest result). Because group 3 is configured\nin single access mode, G3_SamplePtr points always to G3_CH3.\nAdc_GetStreamLastPointer returns the number of valid samples per channel, stored\nin the application result buffer (number of complete group conversion rounds). If the\nreturn value is equal to the configured parameter ’number of streaming samples’, all\nconversion results in the streaming buffer are valid. If the return value is 0, no conver-\nsion results are available in the streaming buffer (the sample pointer will be aligned to\nNULL).\nTo enable Adc_GetStreamLastPointer to align the sample pointer (G1_SamplePtr, G2_\nSamplePtr and G3_SamplePtr) to point to the latest channel result, the API is defined\nto pass a pointer to the result pointer instead the result pointer itself."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "7.3.5 Allocatable Memory Parts\nThe following example shows an Adc driver which is internally split into an interface part\nand a kernel part. ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_STOP_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_16\nNevertheless both memory sections are implemented identical since both are refer-\nencing the identical SwAddrMethod and the MemMapGenericMapping is     {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_4_1_Background",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_ADCDriver",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.4.1 Background\nThe ADC Driver offers power state control APIs and a background elaboration mecha-\nnism to handle asynchronous power state change processes (i.e. power state changes\nwhich are not immediately complete as the they are requested, but need some longer\noperations).\nIt is assumed that all constraints deriving from ECU and SW architecture are already\nsatisfied by the upper layers (Application, Mode Management in the service layer, Io\nHwAbstraction components dealing with peripheral control), thus the scope of control\nis limited to the ADC HW peripheral.\nA check on the operation sequence is executed by the ADC Driver in order to avoid\nrequesting a different power state before the previous request is still being processed\nor activating a power state when no preparation for the same has been requested.\nThe ADC module shall support power control capabilities as an optional function. This\nmodule neither mandates to use only power control enabled MCUs nor to configure\nthe same. Rather it proposes a way to handle power states if this is supported by the\nsuppliers."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "7.4.5 Allocatable Memory Parts\nThe following example shows an Adc driver which is internally split into an interface part\nand a kernel part. Usually the kernel part is allocated to memory with high performance\nfor the micro controller core handling the interrupts. In opposite the interface part is\nusually allocated to memory with a good average performance for all micro controller\ncores using the Adc module.\nVAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_16:\nMemorySection\nsymbol = VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_16\nAdc: BswModuleDescription\ncategory = BSW_MODULE\nAdc_ReadGroup:\nBswCalledEntity\nIbAdc:\nBswInternalBehavior\nCODE_QM_LOCAL:\nSwAddrMethod\nsectionType = code\noption = safetyQM,coreLocal\nAdc:\nBswImplementation\nrcAdc:\nResourceConsumption\nCODE_QM_GLOBAL: MemorySection\nsymbol = CODE_QM_LOCAL\nCODE_QM_LOCAL: MemorySection\nsymbol = CODE_QM_LOCAL\nADC_USERIF: SectionNamePrefix\nsymbol = ADC_USERIF\nADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL: SectionNamePrefix\nsymbol = ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL\nAdc_IsrGroupScanCompleted:\nBswInterruptEntity\nCODE_QM_GLOBAL:\nSwAddrMethod\nsectionType = code\noption = safetyQM,coreGlobal\nVAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL: SwAddrMethod\nsectionType = var\noption = safetyQM,coreLocal\nmemoryAllocationKeywordPolicy = AddrMethodShortNameAndAlignment\nVAR_INIT_QM_GLOBAL_8:\nMemorySection\nsymbol = VAR_INIT_QM_GLOBAL_8\nVAR_INIT_QM_GLOBAL: SwAddrMethod\nsectionType = var\noption = safetyQM,coreGlobal\nmemoryAllocationKeywordPolicy = AddrMethodShortNameAndAlignment\nVAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_8:\nMemorySection\nsymbol = VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_8\n+prefix\n+swAddrmethod\n+swAddrmethod\n+memorySection\n+sectionNamePrefix\n+executableEntity\n+swAddrmethod\n+internalBehavior\n+memorySection\n+prefix\n+memorySection\n+swAddrmethod\n+memorySection\n+memorySection\n+swAddrmethod\n+sectionNamePrefix\n+prefix\n+behavior\n+entity\n+swAddrMethod\n+executableEntity\n+prefix\n+swAddrmethod\n+entity\n+resourceConsumption\n+prefix\nFigure 7.9: Example of description and configuration for allocatable memory parts\nThe shown configuration would result in the support of following Memory Allocation\nKeywords in the Adc_MemMap.h header file:\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_START_SEC_CODE_QM_LOCAL\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_STOP_SEC_CODE_QM_LOCAL\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_START_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_8\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_STOP_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_8\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_START_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_16\n• ADC_AUTOSCANKERNEL_STOP_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_LOCAL_16\n• ADC_USERIF_START_SEC_CODE_QM_GLOBAL\n• ADC_USERIF_STOP_SEC_CODE_QM_GLOBAL\n• ADC_USERIF_START_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_GLOBAL_8\n• ADC_USERIF_STOP_SEC_VAR_INIT_QM_GLOBAL_8\nNevertheless both memory sections are implemented identical since both are refer-\nencing the identical SwAddrMethod and the MemMapGenericMapping is used to\nconfigure the MemMap module."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_5_2_3_Main_function_job_processing_function",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_IOHardwareAbstraction",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.5.2.3 Main function / job processing function\n[SWS_IoHwAb_00035]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00450\n⌈The I/O Hardware Abstraction may contain one or several job processing functions\nthat are BswSchedulableEntities (a sub-class of BswModuleEntity by opposition to\nBswInterruptEntity, e.g. one for each device driver). They shall be activated according\nto their use.\nThey will be time-triggered by the BSW Scheduler. They could be synchronized to the\nexecution of the other runnable entities.\nThe number of BswSchedulableEntities and their order of execution will be implementa-\ntion dependent and must be documented in the I/O Hardware Abstraction description.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_5_2_4_Initialization_De_initialization_and_or_Callout",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_IOHardwareAbstraction",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.5.2.4 Initialization, De-initialization and/or Callout\n[SWS_IoHwAb_00036]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00336, SRS_BSW_00101\n⌈The I/O Hardware Abstraction shall define BswModuleEntries to exchange data with\nother software below the RTE outside interrupt context, for example in case of BSW\ninitialization/de-initialization.⌋\nThese BswModuleEntries are linked to a dedicated BswModuleEntity, which will be\ncalled to perform the service / exchange the data.\nThe I/O Hardware Abstraction may contain one or several initialization and de-\ninitialization functions (e.g. one for each device driver). Similar to the MCAL drivers\nthe initialization functions shall contain a parameter to be able to pass different config-\nurations to the device drivers. This function shall initialize all local and global variables\nused by the I/O Hardware Abstraction driver to an initial state.\n[SWS_IoHwAb_00037] ⌈The initialization/de-initialization functions shall be used/han-\ndled by the ECU State Manager, exclusively. For more information, refer to [9].\nThe number of available functions and the order of execution are implementation-\ndependent and must be documented in the I/O Hardware Abstraction description.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.10 Adc_TriggerSourceType\n[SWS_Adc_00514] Definition of datatype Adc_TriggerSourceType ⌈\nName\nAdc_TriggerSourceType\nKind\nEnumeration\nADC_TRIGG_SRC_SW\n0x00\nGroup is triggered by a software API call.\nRange\nADC_TRIGG_SRC_HW\n0x01\nGroup is triggered by a hardware event.\nDescription\nType for configuring the trigger source for an ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋"

      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.11 Adc_GroupConvModeType\n[SWS_Adc_00515] Definition of datatype Adc_GroupConvModeType ⌈\nName\nAdc_GroupConvModeType\nKind\nEnumeration\nADC_CONV_MODE_\nONESHOT\n0x00\nExactly one conversion of each channel in an\nADC channel group is performed after the\nconfigured trigger event. In case of ’group\ntrigger source software’, a started One-Shot\nconversion can be stopped by a software API\ncall. In case of ’group trigger source\nhardware’, a started One-Shot conversion\ncan be stopped by disabling the trigger event\n(if supported by hardware).\nRange\nADC_CONV_MODE_\nCONTINUOUS\n0x01\nRepeated conversions of each ADC channel\nin an ADC channel group are performed.\n’Continuous conversion mode’ is only\navailable for ’group trigger source software’.\nA started ’Continuous conversion’ can be\nstopped by a software API call.\nDescription\nType for configuring the conversion mode of an ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.15 Adc_StreamBufferModeType\n[SWS_Adc_00519] Definition of datatype Adc_StreamBufferModeType ⌈\nName\nAdc_StreamBufferModeType\nKind\nEnumeration\nADC_STREAM_BUFFER_\nLINEAR\n0x00\nThe ADC Driver stops the conversion as soon\nas the stream buffer is full (number of\nsamples reached).\nRange\nADC_STREAM_BUFFER_\nCIRCULAR\n0x01\nThe ADC Driver continues the conversion\neven if the stream buffer is full (number of\nsamples reached) by wrapping around the\nstream buffer itself.\nDescription\nType for configuring the streaming access mode buffer type.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_2_20_Adc_GroupReplacementType",

      "source_page": 50,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.2.20 Adc_GroupReplacementType\n[SWS_Adc_00523] Definition of datatype Adc_GroupReplacementType ⌈\nName\nAdc_GroupReplacementType\nKind\nEnumeration\nADC_GROUP_REPL_\nABORT_RESTART\n0x00\nAbort/Restart mechanism is used on group\nlevel, if a group is interrupted by a higher\npriority group. The complete conversion\nround of the interrupted group (all group\nchannels)is restarted after the higher priority\ngroup conversion is finished. If the group is\nconfigured in streaming access mode, only\nthe results of the interrupted conversion\nround are discarded. Results of previous\nconversion rounds which are already written\nto the result buffer are not affected.\nRange\nADC_GROUP_REPL_\nSUSPEND_RESUME\n0x01\nSuspend/Resume mechanism is used on\ngroup level, if a group is interrupted by a\nhigher priority group. The conversion round of\nthe interrupted group is completed after the\nhigher priority group conversion is finished.\nResults of previous conversion rounds which\nare already written to the result buffer are not\naffected.\nDescription\nReplacement mechanism, which is used on ADC group level, if a group conversion is interrupted\nby a group which has a higher priority.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.2.9 Adc_StatusType\n[SWS_Adc_00513] Definition of datatype Adc_StatusType ⌈\nName\nAdc_StatusType\nKind\nEnumeration\nADC_IDLE\n0x00\n• The conversion of the specified group has\nnot been started.\n• No result is available.\nADC_BUSY\n0x01\n• The conversion of the specified group has\nbeen started and is still going on.\n• So far no result is available.\nADC_COMPLETED\n0x02\n• A conversion round (which is not the final\none) of the specified group has been\nfinished.\n• A result is available for all channels of the\ngroup.\nRange\nADC_STREAM_\nCOMPLETED\n0x03\n• The result buffer is completely filled\n• For each channel of the selected group the\nnumber of samples to be acquired is\navailable\nDescription\nCurrent status of the conversion of the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋"
    },
    {

      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.10 Adc_DisableGroupNotification\n[SWS_Adc_91004] Definition of API function Adc_DisableGroupNotification ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_DisableGroupNotification\nSyntax\nvoid Adc_DisableGroupNotification (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x08\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nDisables the notification mechanism for the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00058]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_00157, SRS_Adc_12318\n⌈The function Adc_DisableGroupNotification shall disable the notification mechanism\nfor the requested ADC Channel group.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00101]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12447\n⌈The function Adc_DisableGroupNotification shall be pre-compile time configurable\nOn/Off by the configuration parameter AdcGrpNotifCapability⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00131]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the channel group\nID is non-existing, the function Adc_DisableGroupNotification shall raise development\nerror ADC_E_PARAM_GROUP and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00166]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the group notifi-\ncation function pointer is NULL, the function Adc_DisableGroupNotification shall raise\ndevelopment error ADC_E_NOTIF_CAPABILITY and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00300]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called prior to ini-\ntializing the ADC module, Adc_DisableGroupNotification shall raise development error\nADC_E_UNINIT and return without any action.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.11 Adc_GetGroupStatus\n[SWS_Adc_00374] Definition of API function Adc_GetGroupStatus ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_GetGroupStatus\nSyntax\nAdc_StatusType Adc_GetGroupStatus (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x09\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nAdc_StatusType\nConversion status for the requested group.\nDescription\nReturns the conversion status of the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00220]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall return the conversion status of the requested\nADC Channel group.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00221]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00335, SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall return ADC_IDLE:\n• If Adc_GetGroupStatus is called before the conversion of the requested group\nhas been started\n• For groups with trigger source software: If Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after\nthe conversion was stopped with Adc_StopGroupConversion\n• In continuous group conversion mode with linear streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (group was in\nstate ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED while calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer).\n• In continuous group conversion mode with linear streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup (group was in state ADC_\nSTREAM_COMPLETED while calling Adc_ReadGroup).\n• In one-shot SW conversion mode: If Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling\nAdc_GetStreamLastPointer.\n• In one-shot SW conversion mode: If Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling\nAdc_ReadGroup.\n• For groups with trigger source hardware: If Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after\ncalling Adc_DisableHardwareTrigger\n• For groups with trigger source hardware and linear streaming access mode: If\nAdc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (group\nwas in state ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED while calling Adc_GetStreamLast\nPointer).\n• For groups with trigger source hardware and linear streaming access mode: If\nAdc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup (group was in state\nADC_STREAM_COMPLETED while calling Adc_ReadGroup).\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00222]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00335, SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall return ADC_BUSY:\n• If it is called while the first conversion round of the requested group is still ongoing\n(continuous conversion mode).\n• Once trigger is enabled for group with HW trigger source.\n• Once Adc_StartGroupConversion is called for group with SW trigger source.\n• In continuous group conversion mode with single access mode: If Adc_GetGroup\nStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer\n• In continuous group conversion mode with single access mode: If Adc_GetGroup\nStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup.\n• In continuous group conversion mode with circular streaming access mode: If\nAdc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer\n• In continuous group conversion mode with circular streaming access mode If\nAdc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup.\n• In continuous group conversion mode with linear streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (group was in\nstate ADC_COMPLETED while calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer).\n• In continuous group conversion mode with linear streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup (group was in state ADC_\nCOMPLETED while calling Adc_ReadGroup).\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and single access mode: If Adc_GetGroup\nStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer.\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and single access mode: If Adc_GetGroup\nStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup.\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and circular streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer.\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and circular streaming access mode:\nIf Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup.\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and linear streaming access mode: If Adc_\nGetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (group was in\nstate ADC_COMPLETED while calling Adc_GetStreamLastPointer).\n• In one-shot HW conversion mode and linear streaming access mode:\nIf Adc_GetGroupStatus is called after calling Adc_ReadGroup\n(group was in state ADC_COMPLETED while calling Adc_ReadGroup).⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00224]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00335, SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall return ADC_COMPLETED:\n• If it is called after a conversion round (not the final one) of the requested group\nhas been finished.\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00325]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall return ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED:\n• If it is called in single access mode after one conversion round is completed.\n• If it is called in streaming access mode after the number of conversion rounds of\nthe requested group have been finished, to fill the streaming buffer completely.\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00226]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈The function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall provide atomic access to the status data by\nthe use of atomic instructions.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00305] ⌈To guarantee consistent returned values, it is assumed that ADC\ngroup conversion is always started (or enabled in case of HW group) successfully by\nSW before status polling begins.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00225]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the channel group ID\nis non-existing, the function Adc_GetGroupStatus shall raise development error ADC_\nE_PARAM_GROUP and return ADC_IDLE without any action.⌋\n.\n[SWS_Adc_00301]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called prior to initial-\nizing the ADC module, Adc_GetGroupStatus shall raise development error ADC_E_\nUNINIT and return ADC_IDLE without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00436] ⌈In case of an aborted/suspended group, the state of the queued\ngroup remains the same as it was before the group was aborted/suspended.⌋"

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_12_Adc_GetStreamLastPointer",

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.12 Adc_GetStreamLastPointer\n[SWS_Adc_00375] Definition of API function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_GetStreamLastPointer\nSyntax\nAdc_StreamNumSampleType Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (\nAdc_GroupType Group,\nAdc_ValueGroupType** PtrToSamplePtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0b\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nPtrToSamplePtr\nPointer to result buffer pointer.\nReturn value\nAdc_StreamNumSample\nType\nNumber of valid samples per channel.\nDescription\nReturns the number of valid samples per channel, stored in the result buffer. Reads a pointer,\npointing to a position in the group result buffer. With the pointer position, the results of all group\nchannels of the last completed conversion round can be accessed. With the pointer and the\nreturn value, all valid group conversion results can be accessed (the user has to take the layout\nof the result buffer into account).\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00214]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12292, SRS_Adc_12802\n⌈The function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall set the pointer, passed as parameter\n(PtrToSamplePtr) to point in the ADC result buffer to the latest result of the first group\nchannel of the last completed conversion round.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00418] ⌈All values which the ADC driver stores in the ADC result buffer,\nare left without further scaling and shall be aligned according the configuration param-\neter setting of ADC_RESULT_ALIGNMENT.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00387] ⌈The function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall return the number\nof valid samples per channel, stored in the ADC result buffer.⌋\nNote: Valid samples are in the ADC result buffer when the group is in state ADC_\nCOMPLETED or ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED. In state ADC_BUSY or ADC_IDLE\nthe value 0 is returned.\nNote: The return value is 1 for groups with single access mode configuration, if valid\nsamples are stored in the ADC result buffer.\n[SWS_Adc_00216]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12802\n⌈When called while the group status is ADC_BUSY (a conversion of the group is in\nprogress), the function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall set the pointer, passed as pa-\nrameter (PtrToSamplePtr), to NULL and return 0.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00219]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291, SRS_Adc_12802\n⌈The ADC module’s environment shall guarantee the consistency of the data that has\nbeen read by checking the return value of Adc_GetGroupStatus.⌋\nNote: See also SWS_Adc_00140.\n[SWS_Adc_00326]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer while group status is ADC_STREAM_\nCOMPLETED shall trigger a state transition to ADC_BUSY for continuous conversion\nmodes (single access mode or circular streaming buffer mode) and hardware triggered\ngroups in single access mode or circular streaming access mode.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00327]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer while group status is ADC_STREAM_\nCOMPLETED shall trigger a state transition to ADC_IDLE for software conversion\nmodes which automatically stop the conversion (streaming buffer with linear access\nmode or one-shot conversion mode with single access) and for the hardware triggered\nconversion mode in combination with linear streaming access mode.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00328]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer while group status is ADC_COMPLETED\nshall trigger a state transition to ADC_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00215] ⌈When called while the group status is ADC_IDLE and the group\nconversion was not started (no results are available from previous conversions) , the\nfunction Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall report a runtime error ADC_E_IDLE.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00218]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00386\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC moduleis enabled: if the group ID is non-\nexistent, the function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall raise development error ADC_\nE_PARAM_GROUP, set the pointer, passed as parameter (PtrToSamplePtr), to NULL\nand return 0 without any further action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00302]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC moduleis enabled:if called prior to initial-\nizing the driver, the function Adc_GetStreamLastPointer shall raise development error\nADC_E_UNINIT, set the pointer, passed as parameter (PtrToSamplePtr), to NULL and\nreturn 0 without any further action.⌋"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_14_Adc_SetPowerState",

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.14 Adc_SetPowerState\n[SWS_Adc_00475] Definition of API function Adc_SetPowerState ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_SetPowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Adc_SetPowerState (\nAdc_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x10\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: ADC_SERVICE_ACCEPTED: Power\nstate change executed.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: ADC_NOT_INIT: ADC Module not\ninitialized. ADC_SEQUENCE_ERROR: wrong API call sequence.\nADC_HW_FAILURE: the HW module has a failure which\nprevents it to enter the required power state.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Power Mode changed\nE_NOT_OK: request rejected\nDescription\nThis API configures the Adc module so that it enters the already prepared power state, chosen\nbetween a predefined set of configured ones.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00481] ⌈The API configures the HW in order to enter the previously pre-\npared Power State. All preliminary actions to enable this transition (e.g. setting all\nchannels in IDLE status, de-registering of all notifications and so on) must already\nhave been taken by the responsible SWCs (e.g. IoHwAbs).\nThe API shall not execute preliminary, implicit power state changes (i.e. if a requested\npower state is not reachable starting from the current one, no intermediate power state\nchange shall be executed and the request shall be rejected)⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00482] ⌈In case the target power state is the same as the current one, no\naction is executed and the API returns immediately with an E_OK result.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00483] ⌈In case the normal Power State is requested, the API shall refer\nto the necessary parameters contained in the same containers used by Adc_Init.⌋\nNo separate container or hard coded data shall be used for the normal (i.e. full) power\nmode, in order to avoid misalignments between initialization parameters used during\nthe init phase and during a power state change.\n[SWS_Adc_00484] ⌈For the other power states, only power state transition specific\nreconfigurations shall be executed in the context of this API (i.e. the API cannot be used\nto apply a completely new configuration to the Adc module). Any other re-configuration\nnot strictly related to the power state transition shall not take place.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00485] ⌈The API shall refer to the configuration container related to the\nrequired Power State in order to derive some specific features of the state (e.g support\nof Power States).⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00486] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_UNINIT in case this API is called before\nhaving initialized the HW unit.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00487] ⌈The API shall report a runtime error ADC_E_NOT_DISEN-\nGAGED in case this API is called when one or more HW channels (where applicable)\nare in a state different then IDLE (or similar non-operational states) and/or there are\nstill notification registered for the HW module channels.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00488] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_POWER_STATE_NOT_SUPPORTED in\ncase this API is called with an unsupported power state or the peripheral does not\nsupport low power states at all.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00489] ⌈The API shall report a runtime error ADC_E_TRANSITION_\nNOT_POSSIBLE in case the requested power state cannot be directly reached from\nthe current power state.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00490] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_PERIPHERAL_NOT_PREPARED in case\nthe HW unit has not been previously prepared for the target power state by use of the\nAPI Adc_PreparePowerState().⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.16 Adc_GetTargetPowerState\n[SWS_Adc_00477] Definition of API function Adc_GetTargetPowerState ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_GetTargetPowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Adc_GetTargetPowerState (\nAdc_PowerStateType* TargetPowerState,\nAdc_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x12\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nTargetPowerState\nThe Target power mode of the ADC HW Unit is returned in this\nparameter\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: ADC_SERVICE_ACCEPTED:Target\npower mode was returned.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: ADC_NOT_INIT: ADC Module not\ninitialized.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Mode could be read\nE_NOT_OK: Service is rejected\nDescription\nThis API returns the Target power state of the ADC HW unit.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00492] ⌈The API returns the requested power state of the HW unit. This\nshall coincide with the current power state if no transition is ongoing.\nThe API is considered to always succeed except in case of HW failures.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00493] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_UNINIT in case this API is called before\nhaving initialized the HW unit.⌋"

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_17_Adc_PreparePowerState",

      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.17 Adc_PreparePowerState\n[SWS_Adc_00478] Definition of API function Adc_PreparePowerState ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_PreparePowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Adc_PreparePowerState (\nAdc_PowerStateType PowerState,\nAdc_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x13\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nPowerState\nThe target power state intended to be attained\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: ADC_SERVICE_ACCEPTED: ADC\nModule power state preparation was started.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: ADC_NOT_INIT: ADC Module not\ninitialized. ADC_SEQUENCE_ERROR: wrong API call sequence\n(Current Power State = Target Power State). ADC_POWER_\nSTATE_NOT_SUPP: ADC Module does not support the\nrequested power state. ADC_TRANS_NOT_POSSIBLE: ADC\nModule cannot transition directly from the current power state to\nthe requested power state or the HW peripheral is still busy.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Preparation process started\nE_NOT_OK: Service is rejected\nDescription\nThis API starts the needed process to allow the ADC HW module to enter the requested power\nstate.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00494] ⌈This API initiates all actions needed to enable a HW module to\nenter the target power state.\nThe possibility to operate the periphery depends on the power state and the HW fea-\ntures. These properties should be known to the integrator and the decision whether to\nuse the periphery or not is in his responsibility.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00495] ⌈In case the target power state is the same as the current one, no\naction is executed and the API returns immediately with an E_OK result.\nThe responsibility of the preconditions is left to the environment.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00496] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_UNINIT in case this API is called before\nhaving initialized the HW unit.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00497] ⌈In case development error reporting is activated:\nThe API shall report the DET error ADC_E_POWER_STATE_NOT_SUPPORTED in\ncase this API is called with an unsupported power state is requested or the peripheral\ndoes not support low power states at all.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00498] ⌈The API shall report a runtime error ADC_E_TRANSITION_\nNOT_POSSIBLE in case the requested power state cannot be directly reached from\nthe current power state.\nAll asynchronous operation, needed to reach the target power state, can be executed\nin background in the context of Adc_Main_PowerTransitionManager.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.2 Adc_SetupResultBuffer\n[SWS_Adc_91000] Definition of API function Adc_SetupResultBuffer ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_SetupResultBuffer\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Adc_SetupResultBuffer (\nAdc_GroupType Group,\nAdc_ValueGroupType* DataBufferPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0c\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC channel group.\nParameters (in)\nDataBufferPtr\npointer to result data buffer\nParameters (inout)\nNone\n▽\n△\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: result buffer pointer initialized correctly\nE_NOT_OK: operation failed or development error occured\nDescription\nInitializes ADC driver with the group specific result buffer start address where the conversion\nresults will be stored. The application has to ensure that the application buffer, where Data\nBufferPtr points to, can hold all the conversion results of the specified group. The initialization\nwith Adc_SetupResultBuffer is required after reset, before a group conversion can be started.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00420] ⌈The function Adc_SetupResultBuffer shall initialize the result\nbuffer pointer of the selected group with the address value passed as parameter.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00421] ⌈The ADC module’s environment shall ensure that no group con-\nversions are started without prior initialization of the according result buffer pointer to\npoint to a valid result buffer.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00422] ⌈The ADC module’s environment shall ensure that the application\nbuffer, which address is passed as parameter in Adc_SetupResultBuffer, has the ac-\ncording size to hold all group channel conversion results and if streaming access is\nselected, hold these results multiple times as specified with streaming sample param-\neter (see ADC292).⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00423] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if\nthe channel group ID is non-existing, the function Adc_SetupResultBuffer shall raise\ndevelopment error ADC_E_PARAM_GROUP and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00433] ⌈If called while group is not in state ADC_IDLE, function Adc_\nSetupResultBuffer shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00434] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled:\nwhen called prior to initializing the driver, the function Adc_SetupResultBuffer shall\nraise development error ADC_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00457] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled:\nwhen called with a NULL_PTR as DataBufferPtr, the function Adc_SetupResultBuffer\nshall raise development error ADC_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.3 Adc_DeInit\n[SWS_Adc_00366] Definition of API function Adc_DeInit ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_DeInit\nSyntax\nvoid Adc_DeInit (\nvoid\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x01\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nReturns all ADC HW Units to a state comparable to their power on reset state.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00110]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_12163\n⌈The function Adc_DeInit shall return all ADC HW Units to a state comparable to their\npower on reset state. Values of registers which are not writeable are excluded. It’s the\nresponsibility of the hardware design that this state does not lead to undefined activities\nin the µC.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00111]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00336, SRS_SPAL_12163\n⌈The function Adc_DeInit shall disable all used interrupts and notifications.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00358] ⌈The ADC module’s environment shall not call the function Adc_\nDeInit while any group is not in state ADC_IDLE.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00228]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Adc_DeInit shall be pre compile time configurable On/Off by the config-\nuration parameter: AdcDeInitApi.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00112] ⌈If calledwhile not all groups are either in state ADC_IDLE or state\nADC_STREAM_COMPLETED, while no conversion is ongoing (ADC groups which are\nimplicitly stopped), the function Adc_DeInit shall report a runtime error.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00154]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called before the\nmodule has been initialized, the function Adc_DeInit shall raise development error\nADC_E_UNINIT and return without any action.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.4 Adc_StartGroupConversion\n[SWS_Adc_00367] Definition of API function Adc_StartGroupConversion ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_StartGroupConversion\nSyntax\nvoid Adc_StartGroupConversion (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x02\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nStarts the conversion of all channels of the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00061]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12364\n⌈The function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall start the conversion of all channels of\nthe requested ADC Channel group. conversion result storage always starts, after calling Adc_\nStartGroupConversion, at the result buffer base address which was configured with\nAdc_SetupResultBuffer.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00156]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12317, SRS_Adc_12318\n⌈The function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall NOT automatically enable the notifica-\ntion mechanism for that group (this has to be done by a separate API non-\nexisting channel group ID, function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall raise development\nerror ADC_E_PARAM_GROUP and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00133]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: when called on a\ngroup with trigger source configured as hardware, function Adc_StartGroupConversion\nshall raise development error ADC_E_WRONG_TRIGG_SRC and return without any\naction.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00346] ⌈If the priority mechanism is disabled and the queuing is disabled\n: when called while any of the groups, which can not be implicitly stopped, is not in\nstate ADC_IDLE, the function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall report a runtime error\nADC_E_BUSY.⌋\nNote: The condition that any group is not in state ADC_IDLE means in this context:\n• Any conversion is ongoing\nor\n• Any HW trigger is enabled\n[SWS_Adc_00426] ⌈If the priority mechanism is disabled and the queuing is dis-\nabled: when called while any of the groups, which can be implicitly stopped, is not\nin state ADC_IDLE and not in state ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED, the function Adc_\nStartGroupConversion shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\nNote: Groups which can be implicitly stopped are:\n• Software triggered groups configured in one-shot, single-access mode\n• Software triggered groups configured in continuous, linear streaming access\nmode\n• Hardware triggered groups configured in one-shot, linear streaming access mode\n[SWS_Adc_00348] ⌈If the priority mechanism is enabled: when called while agroup,\nwhich can not be implicitly stopped, is not in state ADC_IDLE, the function Adc_Start\nGroupConversion shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\nNote: The condition that the group is not in state ADC_IDLE means in this context:\n• The conversion of the same group is currently ongoing\nor\n• A conversion request for the same group is already stored one time in the queue\n[SWS_Adc_00427] ⌈If the priority mechanism is enabled: when called while a group,\nwhich can be implicitly stopped, is not in state ADC_IDLE and not in state ADC_\nSTREAM_COMPLETED, the function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall report a run-\ntime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00351] ⌈If the priority mechanism is disabled and the queuing is enabled:\nwhen called while a group, which can not be implicitly stopped, is not in state ADC_\nIDLE, the function Adc_StartGroupConversion shall report a runtime error ADC_E_\nBUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00428] ⌈If the priority mechanism is disabled and the queuing is enabled:\nwhen called while a group, which can be implicitly stopped, is not in state ADC_IDLE\nand not in state ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED, the function Adc_StartGroupConver-\nsion shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00294]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled:when called prior to\ninitializing the driver, the (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x03\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters buffer mode), state is ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED\nuntil results are accessed with Adc_ReadGroup or Adc_GetStreamLastPointer API\nfunctions or until group is explicitly stopped by Adc_StopGroupConversion API.\n[SWS_Adc_00295]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called prior to ini-\ntializing the module, function Adc_StopGroupConversion shall raise development error\nADC_E_UNINIT and return without any action.⌋\nNote:\nAll groups which are started with Adc_StartGroupConversion should also be stopped\nwith Adc_StopGroupConversion, before they are started again to reset the group status\nto ADC_IDLE. Exceptions to this rule are groups which are implicitly stopped because\nof the selected conversion mode (linear buffer with streaming access mode or one-\nshot conversion mode with single access).These groups can also be restarted while\nthe group is in state ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED."

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.6 Adc_ReadGroup\n[SWS_Adc_00369] Definition of API function Adc_ReadGroup ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_ReadGroup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Adc_ReadGroup (\nAdc_GroupType Group,\nAdc_ValueGroupType* DataBufferPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x04\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nDataBufferPtr\nADC results of all channels of the selected group are stored in\nthe data buffer addressed with the pointer.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: results are available and written to the data buffer\nE_NOT_OK: no results are available or development error occured\nDescription\nReads the group conversion result of the last completed conversion round of the requested\ngroup and stores the channel values starting at the DataBufferPtr address. The group channel\nvalues are stored in ascending channel number order ( in contrast to the storage layout of the\nresult buffer if streaming access is configured).\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00075] ⌈The function Adc_ReadGroup shall read the latest available con-\nversion results of the requested group.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00113]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_12063,\nSRS_Adc_12819,\nSRS_Adc_12292,\nSRS_Adc_-\n12824\n⌈The function Adc_ReadGroup shall read the raw converted values without further\nscaling. The read values shall be aligned according the configuration parameter setting\nof ADC_RESULT_ALIGNMENT.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00122]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12283, SRS_Adc_12819\n⌈If applicable, the function Adc_ReadGroup shall mask out all information or diagnos-\ntic bits provided by the conversion but not belonging to the conversion results them-\nselves.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00329]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_ReadGroup while group status is ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED\nshall trigger a state transition to ADC_BUSY for continuous conversion modes (single\naccess mode or circular streaming buffer mode) and hardware triggered groups in\nsingle access mode or circular streaming access mode.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00330]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_ReadGroup while group status is ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED\nshall trigger a state transition to ADC_IDLE for software triggered conversion modes\nwhich automatically stop the conversion (streaming buffer with linear access mode or\none-shot conversion mode with single access) and for the hardware triggered conver-\nsion mode in combination with linear streaming access mode.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00331]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12291\n⌈Calling function Adc_ReadGroup while group status is ADC_COMPLETED shall trig-\nger a state transition to ADC_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00359] ⌈The function Adc_ReadGroup shall be pre-compile configurable\nOn/Off by the configuration parameter AdcReadGroupApi.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00388] ⌈When called while the group status is ADC_IDLE and the group\nconversion was not started (no results are available from previous conversions), the\nfunction Adc_ReadGroup shall report a runtime error ADC_E_IDLE.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00152]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the group ID is non-\nexisting, the function Adc_ReadGroup shall raise development error ADC_E_PARAM_\nGROUP and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00296] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled:\nwhen called prior to initializing the driver, the function Adc_ReadGroup shall raise de-\nvelopment error ADC_E_UNINIT and return E_NOT_OK.⌋"
