      "verbatim_text": "8.3.7 Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger\n[SWS_Adc_91001] Definition of API function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_EnableHardwareTrigger\nSyntax\nvoid Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x05\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\n▽\n△\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nEnables the hardware trigger for the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00114]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12823\n⌈The function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall enable the hardware trigger for the\nrequested ADC Channel group.⌋\nNote: Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger can only be used for ADC internal trigger sources\ncontrolled from the ADC hardware.\n[SWS_Adc_00144]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12823\n⌈A group with trigger source hardware, whose trigger was enabled with Adc_Enable\nHardwareTrigger, shall execute the group channel conversions, whenever a trigger\nevent occurs.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00432] ⌈The function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall reset the internal\ngroup result buffer pointer, that conversion result storage always starts, after calling\nAdc_EnableHardwareTrigger, at the result buffer base address which was configured\nwith Adc_SetupResultBuffer.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00273]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12823\n⌈The ADC module’s environment shall guarantee that no concurrent conversions take\nplace on the same HW Unit (happening of different hardware triggers at the same\ntime).⌋\nNote: The reason for SWS_Adc_00273 is that the ADC module can only handle one\ngroup conversion request per HW Unit at the same time. In case of concurrent HW\nconversion requests, the HW prioritization mechanism controls the conversion order.\n[SWS_Adc_00120]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The ADC module’s environment shall only call the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrig-\nger for groups configured in hardware trigger mode (see AdcGroupTriggSrc).⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00265]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall be pre-compile time configurable On/\nOff by the configuration parameter AdcHwTriggerApi.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00321] ⌈If the priority mechanism is disabled and queuing disabled: when\ncalled while any group with trigger source SW is not in state ADC_IDLE, the function\nAdc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00349] ⌈If the HW trigger for the group is already enabled, the function\nAdc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00353] ⌈If the maximum number of available hardware triggers is already\nenabled (device and implementation specific), the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrig-\nger shall report a runtime error ADC_E_BUSY.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00128]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the channel group\nID is invalid, the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall raise development error\nADC_E_PARAM_GROUP and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00136]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the group is con-\nfigured for software API trigger mode, the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall\nraise development error ADC_E_WRONG_TRIGG_SRC and return without any ac-\ntion.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00281]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12823\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if a HW group is er-\nroneously configured for continuous conversion mode, the function Adc_EnableHard-\nwareTrigger shall raise development error ADC_E_WRONG_CONV_MODE and return\nwithout any action.⌋\nNote: SW groups configured in continuous conversion mode shall raise development\nerror ADC_E_WRONG_TRIGG_SRC instead.\n[SWS_Adc_00297]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called prior to ini-\ntializing the driver, the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall raise development\nerror ADC_E_UNINIT and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00425] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled:\nwhen called prior to initializing the result buffer pointer with function Adc_SetupResult\nBuffer, the function Adc_EnableHardwareTrigger shall raise development error ADC_\nE_BUFFER_UNINIT.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.9 Adc_EnableGroupNotification\n[SWS_Adc_91003] Definition of API function Adc_EnableGroupNotification ⌈\nService Name\nAdc_EnableGroupNotification\nSyntax\nvoid Adc_EnableGroupNotification (\nAdc_GroupType Group\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nGroup\nNumeric ID of requested ADC Channel group.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nEnables the notification mechanism for the requested ADC Channel group.\nAvailable via\nAdc.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00057]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_00157, SRS_Adc_12318\n⌈The function Adc_EnableGroupNotification shall enable the notification mechanism\nfor the requested ADC Channel group.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00100]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Adc_12447\n⌈The function Adc_EnableGroupNotification shall be pre-compile time configurable On/\nOff by the configuration parameter AdcGrpNotifCapability.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00130] ⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if\nthe channel group ID is non-existing, the function Adc_EnableGroupNotification shall\nraise development error ADC_E_PARAM_GROUP and return without any action.⌋\n(SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448, )\n[SWS_Adc_00165]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00386, SRS_SPAL_12448\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if the group notifi-\ncation function pointer is NULL, the function Adc_EnableGroupNotification shall raise\ndevelopment error ADC_E_NOTIF_CAPABILITY and return without any action.⌋\n[SWS_Adc_00299]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00406\n⌈If development error detection for the ADC module is enabled: if called prior to ini-\ntializing the ADC module, Adc_EnableGroupNotification shall raise development error\nADC_E_UNINIT and return without any action.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.6.3.2 IoHwAb_Adc_NotifyReadyForPowerState<#Mode>\n[SWS_Adc_00480]\nDefinition of configurable interface IoHwAb_Adc_Notify\nReadyForPowerState<#Mode> ⌈\nService Name\nIoHwAb_Adc_NotifyReadyForPowerState<#Mode>\nSyntax\nvoid IoHwAb_Adc_NotifyReadyForPowerState<#Mode> (\nvoid\n)\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThe API shall be invoked by the ADC Driver when the requested power state preparation for\nmode <#Mode> is completed.\nAvailable via\nIoHwAb_Adc.h\n⌋\nThis interface provided by CDD or IoHwAbs controlling the peripheral is needed if at\nleast one MCAL driver is configured for providing power mode control APIs.\nThere shall be one such a callback for each power mode in which the ADC has to\nchange power state. It is possible to have the same power state for different power\nmodes, but only one power state for a given power mode."
    },

      "evidence_status": "verified",
      "guideline": "Normativ verbindlicher Beleg (🔒 Verifizierter Kontext)",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 4.1: Image of the PWM channel for diagnosis [SRS_Pwm_12297] The PWM driver shall provide a service for setting the period of a selected channel ⌈ Description: The PWM driver shall provide a service for setting the period of a selected channel. The parameters shall be • PWM channel • PWM period • PWM duty cycle This functionality is available only for the PWM channel configured as type of channels \"Variable Period\". Rationale: The PWM duty cycle parameter is necessary to maintain the consistency between frequency and duty cycle. Otherwise, the effective duty cycle would change when the period is validor the PWM driver would have to recalculate the valid duty cycle by itself. ▽"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.7: Use case of output power stage Some outputs are controlled via the SPI driver/handler. Some inputs are directly controlled via the DIO driver.     {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_2_2_6_Concurrency_safe_implementation_of_modules",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "EXP_BSWDistributionGuide",
      "source_page": 18,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "2.2.6 Concurrency safe implementation of modules\nConcurrency safety of BSW modules respectively the functions implemented by these\nmodules may be achieved by different mechanisms.\nGenerally, the following levels of reentrancy can be distinguished according to [TPS_\nBSWMDT_04103]. The concrete level of a BswModuleEntity is defined in the op-\ntional attribute \"reentrancyLevel\".\n• Multi-core reentrant: Unlimited concurrent execution of an interface is possible,\nincluding preemption and parallel execution on multi-core systems. This level can\nbe either achieved by mutual exclusion when entering critical regions, or by the\nabsence of such regions, for example if there are no shared resources (including\nhardware and memory).\n• Single-core reentrant: Pseudo-concurrent execution (i.e. preemption) of an in-\nterface is possible on single core systems. This is the highest level of reentrancy\ndefined by AUTOSAR 4.0.3. Because it does not explicitly cover multi-core sys-\ntems, \"concurrency safe\" has been introduced additionally. This level can gener-\nally be ensured by the same mechanisms as \"concurrency safe\", but they must\nbe ensured to work across core boundaries.\n• Non-reentrant: Concurrent execution of this interface is not possible.\nIf a module that is not concurrency safe is invoked in different partitions, there is no\nwarranty that the module will uphold its desired behavior. In this case, correct behavior\nshall be ensured by the usage of the module, for example if the caller(s) prevent parallel\nexecution by using exclusive areas."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_2_2_7_Kernel_based_Master_Satellite_Realization",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "EXP_BSWDistributionGuide",
      "source_page": 18,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "2.2.7 Kernel based Master-Satellite Realization\nOne way of realizing the master-satellite concept is the implementation of a module\nsplit into kernel and according interfaces, which are provided for all partitions the mod-\nule shall be used from. The focus of the chapter is to describe the idea of the distribu-\ntion of the according BSW module as a guidance for similar cases.\nIn a first step the service API’s are categorized, e.g. according to MCAL distribution\nconcept:\n• Service API required by multiple cores / partitions for triggering and reading /\nwriting of data\n• Service API which are required by one partition only (e.g. initialization, shutdown)\nThis will lead to the following BSW module architecture:\nFigure 2.3\nIn the second step the SW designer needs to select an according BSW distribution\npattern for each service API following the below listed categories:\n• Trigger a control flow from service API to kernel API (if required including data)\n• Read of a symbol from a global buffer\n• Write a symbol to a global buffer, which is later-on polled by the kernel\nGuide to BSW Distribution\nFor reading and writing data, one will typically implement according get and set oper-\nations into the interface part of the BSW module, adding an according data protection\nmean (e.g. spinlock) if necessary.\nFor transferring control flow, one will implement on the one hand side the user API\noperation and on the other hand the same operation inside the kernel API. The relation\ncan be 1:1 (one user API matches one kernel API) or n:1 (several user API match one\nkernel API).\nAll local API have to be allocated with local core scope and all global API with global\ncore scope applying the memory allocation specification (AUTOSAR_SWS_Memory\nMapping, see [2]).\nApplying this idea to the PWM driver, one would get the following API distribution:\nControl API with local scope:\nCONTROL API\nCore Scope\nPwm_Init\nlocal (same partition as kernel)\nPwm_DeInit\nlocal (same partition as kernel)\nPwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager\nlocal (same partition as kernel)\nNote that these API’s are restricted to the local kernel partition. The task calling the\ntransition manager needs to be scheduled within the same partition / on the same core.\nUser read/write API with global scope:\nUSER_RW API\nAccess / Core Scope\nPwm_GetOutputState\nread global data\nPwm_GetCurrentPowerState\nread global data\nPwm_GetTargetPowerState\nread global data\nPwm_GetVersionInfo\nread static information\nPwm_DisableNotification\nwrite to global data (atomic flag)\nPwm_EnableNotification\nwrite to global data (atomic flag)\nNote that these API’s are available to any partition, so these are also used if the call is\ndone from the same partition where the kernel resides.\nUser trigger API with global scope and related kernel API with local scope:\nUSER_TRIG_API / Global Scope\nKERNEL_API / Local Scope\nPwm_SetDutyCycle\nPwm_SetPeriodAndDuty\nPwm_Kernel_SetValues\nPwm_SetOutputToIdle\nPwm_Kernel_SetOutputToIdle\nPwm_SetPowerState\nPwm_PreparePowerState\nPwm_Kernel_PowerStateManager\nNote that the USER_TRIG_API is available to any partition, so these are also used\nif the call is done from the same partition where the kernel resides. The KERNEL_\nGuide to BSW Distribution\nAPI however is not accessible to the user. It is internal only. The calls from the local\npartition are passed through the USER_TRIG_API.\nFinally, the picture below shall summarize the interface availability along the cores /\npartitions for the given example, while the kernel API is hidden inside the BSW module\nnot visible to the outside.\nFigure 2.4\nThe following points shall be noted in addition:\n• All user callbacks shall be called in the local partition. The user needs then to\nprovide similarly a service API with global scope, which can be called. This is\nuseful as the implementer of each BSW module or CDD knows ideally how its\nmodule is designed. Doing the other way around could waste CPU resources\ninstead as caller and called module might implement the partition transfer twice.\n• It is strongly not recommended to apply this or other master-satellite concepts for\ncrossing partitions on the same core, e.g. motivated by safety, as this will also\nwaste CPU resources.\nWhen choosing the according protection and multi-core means one shall always try\nto achieve a blockade free implementation to allow parallel operation along multiple\ncores.\nGuide to BSW Distribution"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "2 Acronyms and abbreviations\nAcronyms and abbreviations that have a local scope are not contained in the\nAUTOSAR glossary. These must appear in a local glossary.\nAcronym:\nDescription:\nPWM Channel\nNumeric identifier linked to a hardware PWM.\nPWM Output\nState\nDefines the output state for a PWM signal. It could be:\n\nHigh.\n\nLow.\nPWM Idle State\nThe idle state represents the output state of the PWM channel after the call of\nPwm_SetOutputToIdle or Pwm_DeInit\nPWM Polarity\nDefines the starting output state of each PWM channel\nPWM Duty cycle\nDefines a percentage of the starting level (could be high or low) related to the\nperiod.\nPWM period\nDefines the period of the PWM signal.\nAbbreviation: Description:\nPWM\nPulse Width Modulation.\nDEM\nDiagnostic Event Manager.\nDET\nDefault Error Tracer.\nMCU\nMicrocontroller Unit.\nPLL\nPhase Locked Loop.\nISR\nInterrupt Service Routine."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_7_3_1_Background",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.1 Background\nThe PWM Driver offers power state control APIs and a background elaboration mecha-\nnism to handle asynchronous power state change processes (i.e. power state changes\nwhich are not immediately complete as the they are requested, but need some longer\noperations).\nIt is assumed that all constraints deriving from ECU and SW architecture are already\nsatisfied by the upper layers (Application, Mode Management in the service layer, Io-\nHwAbstraction components dealing with peripheral control), thus the scope of control\nis limited to the PWM HW peripheral.\nA check on the operation sequence is executed by the PWM Driver in order to avoid\nrequesting a different power state before the previous request is still being processed\nor activating a power state when no preparation for the same has been requested.\nThe PWM module shall support power control capabilities as an optional function. This\nmodule neither mandates to use only power control enabled MCUs nor to configure\nthe same. Rather it proposes a way to handle power states if this is supported by the\nsuppliers."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_7_3_2_Requirements",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.2 Requirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00154]  ⌈The PwmDriver shall support power state changes and its\nAPIs when the corresponding configuration parameter\nPwmLowPowerStatesSupport is set to TRUE.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00155] ⌈If the parameter PwmLowPowerStatesSupport is enabled\nthen the APIs Pwm_PreparePowerState, Pwm_SetPowerState,\nPwm_GetCurrentPowerState, Pwm_GetTargetPowerState shall be\ngenerated and shall be used to manage and get informations on power state\ntransitions.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00156] ⌈The APIs Pwm_GetTargetPowerState and\nPwm_GetCurrentPowerState shall be respectively used to gather information on\nthe requested and the target Pwm power states.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00157] ⌈The API Pwm_PreparePowerState shall be used to start a\npower state transition. ⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00158] ⌈After preparation for a power state is achieved by\n([SWS_Pwm_00157]) then the API Pwm_SetPowerState  shall be  used to achieve\nthe requested power state of the Pwm module.\nIn order to avoid incoherent power state conditions, some APIs\n(Pwm_SetPowerState, Pwm_PreparePowerState) have to be called in a given\nsequence, otherwise an error (if DET tracing is enabled) is stored and the action is\ninterrupted. The Pwm Driver keeps track of the call sequence.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00159] ⌈The Pwm Driver shall keep track of the call order of the APIs\nPwm_SetPowerState and Pwm_PreparePowerState. In case the first one is\ncalled before the second one is called, a DET entry shall be stored and the action\nshall not be executed.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00160] ⌈The Pwm Module shall keep track of the current and of the\ntarget  powerstate if the parameter PwmLowPowerStatesSupport  is set to TRUE⌋\n().\n[SWS_Pwm_00161]  ⌈After the Initiliazation the power state of the module shall be\nalways FULL POWER if the PwmLowPowerStatesSupport is set to TRUE.⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00162]  ⌈The Pwm Driver shall support synchronuous and\nasynchronous power state transitions, depending on the value of the configuration\nparameter PwmPowerStateAsynchTransitionMode. ⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00163] ⌈In case the configuration parameter\nPwmPowerStateAsynchTransitionMode is set to FALSE, the preparation process and\nthe setting process shall be considered concluded as soon as the respective APIs\nreturn. ⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00164] ⌈In case the configuration parameter\nPwmPowerStateAsynchTransitionMode is set to TRUE, the preparation process shall\ncontinue in background after the relative API returns and its completion shall be\nnotified by means of the configured callback.⌋()"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_7_4_Duty_Cycle_Resolution_and_scaling",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 18,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.4 Duty Cycle Resolution and scaling\n[SWS_Pwm_00058]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12383\n⌈The width of the duty cycle parameter is 16 Bits.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00059]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12459\n⌈The Pwm module shall comply with the following scaling scheme for the duty cycle:\n• 0x0000 means 0%.\n• 0x8000 means 100%. 0x8000 gives the highest resolution while allowing 100%\nduty cycle to be represented with a 16 bit value.\nAs an implementation guide, the following source code example is given:\nAbsoluteDutyCycle = ((uint32)AbsolutePeriodTime * RelativeDutyCycle) >> 15;\n⌋"
    },
    {

      "source_element": null,

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.10 Pwm_GetCurrentPowerState\n[SWS_Pwm_00177] Definition of API function Pwm_GetCurrentPowerState ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_GetCurrentPowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Pwm_GetCurrentPowerState (\nPwm_PowerStateType* CurrentPowerState,\nPwm_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0a\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nCurrentPowerState\nThe current power mode of the PWM HW Unit is returned in this\nparameter\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: PWM_SERVICE_ACCEPTED: Current\npower mode was returned.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: PWM_NOT_INIT: PWM Module\nnot initialized.\n▽\n△\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Mode could be read\nE_NOT_OK: Service is rejected\nDescription\nThis API returns the current power state of the PWM HW unit.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00178] ⌈The API returns the power state of the HW unit.⌋\nIn case development error reporting is activated:\n[SWS_Pwm_00179] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_UNINIT in\ncase this API is called before having initialized the HW unit.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_11_Pwm_GetTargetPowerState",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.11 Pwm_GetTargetPowerState\n[SWS_Pwm_00180] Definition of API function Pwm_GetTargetPowerState ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_GetTargetPowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Pwm_GetTargetPowerState (\nPwm_PowerStateType* TargetPowerState,\nPwm_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0b\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nTargetPowerState\nThe Target power mode of the PWM HW Unit is returned in this\nparameter\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: PWM_SERVICE_ACCEPTED:Target\npower mode was returned.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: PWM_NOT_INIT: PWM Module\nnot initialized.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Mode could be read\nE_NOT_OK: Service is rejected\nDescription\nThis API returns the Target power state of the PWM HW unit.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00181] ⌈The API returns the requested power state of the HW unit. This\nshall coincide with the current power state if no transition is ongoing.\nThe API is considered to always succeed except in case of HW failures.⌋\nIn case development error reporting is activated:\n[SWS_Pwm_00182] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_UNINIT in\ncase this API is called before having initialized the HW unit.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_12_Pwm_PreparePowerState",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.12 Pwm_PreparePowerState\n[SWS_Pwm_00183] Definition of API function Pwm_PreparePowerState ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_PreparePowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Pwm_PreparePowerState (\nPwm_PowerStateType PowerState,\nPwm_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0c\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nPowerState\nThe target power state intended to be attained\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: PWM_SERVICE_ACCEPTED: PWM\nModule power state preparation was started.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: PWM_NOT_INIT: PWM Module\nnot initialized. PWM_SEQUENCE_ERROR: wrong API call\nsequence (Current Power State = Target Power State). PWM_\nPOWER_STATE_NOT_SUPP: PWM Module does not support\nthe requested power state. PWM_TRANS_NOT_POSSIBLE:\nPWM Module cannot transition directly from the current power\nstate to the requested power state or the HW peripheral is still\nbusy.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Preparation process started\nE_NOT_OK: Service is rejected\nDescription\nThis API starts the needed process to allow the PWM HW module to enter the requested power\nstate.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00184] ⌈This API initiates all actions needed to enable a HW module to\nenter the target power state.\nThe possibility to operate the periphery depends on the power state and the HW fea-\ntures. These properties should be known to the integrator and the decision whether to\nuse the periphery or not is in his responsibility.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00185] ⌈In case the target power state is the same as the current one,\nno action is executed and the API returns immediately with an E_OK result.\nThe responsibility of the preconditions is left to the environment.⌋\nIn case development error reporting is activated:\n[SWS_Pwm_00186] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_UNINIT in\ncase this API is called before having initialized the HW unit.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00187] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_POWER_-\nSTATE_NOT_SUPPORTED in case this API is called with an unsupported power state is\nrequested or the peripheral does not support low power states at all.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00188]\n⌈The\nAPI\nshall\nreport\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nPWM_E_-\nTRANSITION_NOT_POSSIBLE in case the requested power state cannot be directly\nreached from the current power state.\nAll asynchronous operation needed to reach the target power state can be executed in\nbackground in the context of Pwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.2 Pwm_DeInit\n[SWS_Pwm_00096] Definition of API function Pwm_DeInit ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_DeInit\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_DeInit (\nvoid\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x01\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\n▽\n△\nDescription\nService for PWM De-Initialization.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00010]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00336, SRS_SPAL_12163, SRS_Pwm_12381\n⌈The function Pwm_DeInit shall de-initialize the PWM module.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00011]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_12163\n⌈The function Pwm_DeInit shall set the state of the PWM output signals to the idle\nstate.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00012]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_SPAL_12163\n⌈The function Pwm_DeInit shall disable PWM interrupts and PWM signal edge notifi-\ncations.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10080]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_DeInit shall be pre compile time configurable On/Off by the con-\nfiguration parameter: PwmDeInitApi.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20080]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_DeInit shall be configurable On/Off by the configuration parame-\nter PwmDeInitApi {PWM_DE_INIT_API}.\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051],\nand [SWS_Pwm_20051] are applicable to the function\nPwm_DeInit.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.3 Pwm_SetDutyCycle\n[SWS_Pwm_91000] Definition of API function Pwm_SetDutyCycle ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_SetDutyCycle\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_SetDutyCycle (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber,\nuint16 DutyCycle\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x02\n▽\n△\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\nParameters (in)\nDutyCycle\nMin=0x0000 Max=0x8000\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nService sets the duty cycle of the PWM channel.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00013]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12295\n⌈The function Pwm_SetDutyCycle shall set the duty cycle of the PWM channel.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00014] ⌈When the requested duty cycle is either 0% or 100%, the func-\ntion\nPwm_SetDutyCycle shall set the PWM output state to either PWM_HIGH or PWM_LOW,\nwith regard to both the configured polarity parameter and the requested duty cycle.\nThus for 0% requested Duty Cycle the output will be the inverse of the configured\npolarity parameter, and for 100% Duty Cycle the output will be equal to the configured\npolarity parameter.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00016] ⌈The function Pwm_SetDutyCycle shall modulate the PWM out-\nput signal according to parameters period, duty cycle and configured polarity, when the\nduty cycle > 0 % and < 100%.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00017]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12382\n⌈The function Pwm_SetDutyCycle shall update the duty cycle always at the end of\nthe period if supported by the implementation and configured with PwmDutycycleUp-\ndatedEndperiod.⌋\nRegarding\nformat\ndefinition\nof\nduty\ncycle\nparameter,\nthe\nrequirement\n[SWS_Pwm_00058] is applicable to the function Pwm_SetDutyCycle.\nRegarding\nscaling\ndefinition\nof\nduty\ncycle\nparameter,\nthe\nrequirement\n[SWS_Pwm_00059] is applicable to the function Pwm_SetDutyCycle.\n[SWS_Pwm_00018] ⌈The driver shall forbid the spike on the PWM output signal.⌋\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051]\nare\napplica-\nble to the function Pwm_SetDutyCycle.\n[SWS_Pwm_10082]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetDutyCycle shall be pre compile time configurable On/Off by\nthe configuration parameter: PwmSetDutyCycle.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20082]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetDutyCycle shall be configurable On/Off by the configuration\nparameter: PwmSetDutyCycle {PWM_SET_DUTY_CYCLE_API}.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.4 Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty\n[SWS_Pwm_91001] Definition of API function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_SetPeriodAndDuty\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber,\nPwm_PeriodType Period,\nuint16 DutyCycle\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x03\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\nPeriod\nPeriod of the PWM signal\nParameters (in)\nDutyCycle\nMin=0x0000 Max=0x8000\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nService sets the period and the duty cycle of a PWM channel\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00019]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12297\n⌈The function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty shall set the period and the duty cycle of a\nPWM channel.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00076] ⌈The function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty shall update the period\nalways at the end of the current period if supported by the implementation and config-\nured with PwmPeriodUpdatedEndperiod.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00020] ⌈When updating the PWM period and duty, the driver shall re-\npress any spikes on the PWM output signal.⌋\nThe PWM duty cycle parameter is necessary to maintain the consistency between\nfrequency and duty cycle. Refer to [SWS_Pwm_00058] and [SWS_Pwm_00059] to\nknow the scaling and format definition of duty cycle parameter\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00045],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051] are applicable to the function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty.\n[SWS_Pwm_00041]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12389\n⌈The function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty shall allow changing the period only for the\nPWM channel declared as variable Period type.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10083]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty shall be pre compile time configurable\nOn/Off by the configuration parameter: PwmSetPeriodAndDuty.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20083]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty shall be configurable On/Off by the configu-\nration parameter: PwmSetPeriodAndDuty {PWM_SET_PERIOD_AND_DUTY_API}.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00150] ⌈If the period is set to zero the setting of the duty-cycle is not\nrelevant. In this case the output shall be zero (zero percent duty-cycle).⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.5 Pwm_SetOutputToIdle\n[SWS_Pwm_91002] Definition of API function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_SetOutputToIdle\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_SetOutputToIdle (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x04\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nParameters (in)\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nService sets the PWM output to the configured Idle state.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00021]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12358\n⌈The function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle shall set immediately the PWM output to the\nconfigured Idle state.⌋\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051]\nare\napplica-\nble to the function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle.\n[SWS_Pwm_10084]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle shall be pre compile time configurable On/Off\nby the configuration parameter: PwmSetOutputToIdle.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20084]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle shall be configurable On/Off by the configura-\ntion parameter: PwmSetOutputToIdle {PWM_SET_OUTPUT_TO_IDLE_API}.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10086] ⌈After the call of the function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle, variable\nperiod type channels shall be reactivated using the Api Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty to\nactivate the PWM channel with the new passed period.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20086] ⌈After the call of the function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle, channels\nshall be reactivated using the Api Pwm_SetDutyCycle to activate the PWM channel\nwith the old period.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00119] ⌈After the call of the function Pwm_SetOutputToIdle, fixed pe-\nriod type channels shall be reactivated using only the API Pwm_SetDutyCycle to\nactivate the PWM channel with the old period.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.6 Pwm_GetOutputState\n[SWS_Pwm_00100] Definition of API function Pwm_GetOutputState ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_GetOutputState\nSyntax\nPwm_OutputStateType Pwm_GetOutputState (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x05\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nParameters (in)\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\n▽\n△\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nPwm_OutputStateType\nPWM_HIGH The PWM output state is high\nPWM_LOW The PWM output state is low\nDescription\nService to read the internal state of the PWM output signal.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00022]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12385\n⌈The function Pwm_GetOutputState shall read the internal state of the PWM output\nsignal and return it as defined in the diagram below.\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051]\nare\napplica-\nble to the function Pwm_GetOutputState.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10085]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_GetOutputState shall be pre compile time configurable On/Off\nusing the configuration parameter: PwmGetOutputState.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20085]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00171\n⌈The function Pwm_GetOutputState shall be configurable On/Off by the configura-\ntion parameter: PwmGetOutputState {PWM_GET_OUTPUT_STATE_API}.\nDue to real time constraint and setting of the PWM channel (project dependant), the\noutput state can be modified just after the call of the service Pwm_GetOutputState.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_30051]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386\n⌈If Pwm_GetOutputState is called before module initialization, or with an invalid\nchannel, it shall return PWM_LOW.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.7 Pwm_DisableNotification\n[SWS_Pwm_91003] Definition of API function Pwm_DisableNotification ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_DisableNotification\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_DisableNotification (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x06\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nParameters (in)\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nService to disable the PWM signal edge notification.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00023]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12378, SRS_Pwm_12299\n⌈The function Pwm_DisableNotification shall disable the PWM signal edge noti-\nfication.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10112] ⌈The function Pwm_DisableNotification shall be pre com-\npile time configurable On/Off using the configuration parameter: PwmNotification-\nSupported.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20112] ⌈The function Pwm_DisableNotification shall be con-\nfigurable On/Off by the configuration parameter:\nPwmNotificationSupported\n{PWM_NOTIFICATION_SUPPORTED}.\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051]\nare\napplica-\nble to the function Pwm_DisableNotification.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.8 Pwm_EnableNotification\n[SWS_Pwm_91004] Definition of API function Pwm_EnableNotification ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_EnableNotification\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_EnableNotification (\nPwm_ChannelType ChannelNumber,\nPwm_EdgeNotificationType Notification\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant for different channel numbers\nChannelNumber\nNumeric identifier of the PWM\nParameters (in)\nNotification\nType of notification PWM_RISING_EDGE or PWM_FALLING_\nEDGE or PWM_BOTH_EDGES\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nService to enable the PWM signal edge notification according to notification parameter.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00024]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Pwm_12378, SRS_Pwm_12299\n⌈The function Pwm_EnableNotification shall enable the PWM signal edge notifi-\ncation according to notification parameter.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00081] ⌈The function Pwm_EnableNotification shall cancel pending\ninterrupts.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_10113] ⌈The function Pwm_EnableNotification shall be pre compile\ntime configurable On/Off using the configuration parameter: PwmNotificationSup-\nported.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_20113] ⌈The function Pwm_EnableNotification shall be config-\nurable On/Off by the configuration parameter:\nPwmNotificationSupported\n{PWM_NOTIFICATION_SUPPORTED}.\nRegarding\nerror\ndetection,\nthe\nrequirements\n[SWS_Pwm_00117],\n[SWS_Pwm_00047],\n[SWS_Pwm_10051]\nand\n[SWS_Pwm_20051]\nare\napplica-\nble to the function Pwm_EnableNotification.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_9_Pwm_SetPowerState",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_PWMDriver",
      "source_page": 36,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.9 Pwm_SetPowerState\n[SWS_Pwm_00166] Definition of API function Pwm_SetPowerState ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_SetPowerState\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Pwm_SetPowerState (\nPwm_PowerStateRequestResultType* Result\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x09\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nResult\nIf the API returns E_OK: PWM_SERVICE_ACCEPTED:Power\nstate change executed.\nIf the API returns E_NOT_OK: PWM_NOT_INIT: PWM Module\nnot initialized. PWM_SEQUENCE_ERROR: wrong API call\nsequence. PWM_HW_FAILURE: the HW module has a failure\nwhich prevents it to enter the required power state.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: Power Mode changed\nE_NOT_OK: request rejected\nDescription\nThis API configures the Pwm module so that it enters the already prepared power state, chosen\nbetween a predefined set of configured ones.\nAvailable via\nPwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00167] ⌈The API configures the HW in order to enter the given Power\nState. All preliminary actions to enable this transition (e.g. setting all channels in IDLE\nstatus, de-registering of all notifications and so on) must already have been taken by\nthe responsible SWCs (e.g. IoHwAbs).\nThe API shall not execute preliminary, implicit power state changes (i.e. if a requested\npower state is not reachable starting from the current one, no intermediate power state\nchange shall be executed and the request shall be rejected).⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00168] ⌈In case the target power state is the same as the current one,\nno action is executed and the API returns immediately with an E_OK result.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00169] ⌈In case the normal Power State is requested, the API shall refer\nto the necessary parameters contained in the same containers used by Pwm_Init.\nNo separate container or hard coded data shall be used for the normal (i.e. full) power\nmode, in order to avoid misalignments between initialization parameters used during\nthe init phase and during a power state change.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00170] ⌈For the other power states, only power state transition specific\nreconfigurations shall be executed in the context of this API (i.e. the API cannot be\nused to apply a completely new configuration to the Pwm module).\nAny other re-\nconfiguration not strictly related to the power state transition shall not take place.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00171] ⌈The API shall refer to the configuration container related to the\nrequired Power State in order to derive some specific features of the state (e.g support\nof Power States).⌋\nIn case development error reporting is activated:\n[SWS_Pwm_00172] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_UNINIT in\ncase this API is called before having initialized the HW unit.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00173] ⌈The API shall report the runtime error PWM_E_NOT_DISEN-\nGAGED in case this API is called when one or more HW channels (where applicable)\nare in a state different than IDLE (or similar non-operational states) and/or there are\nstill notification registered for the HW module channels.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00194] ⌈The API shall report the development error PWM_E_POWER_-\nSTATE_NOT_SUPPORTED in case this API is called with an unsupported power state\nor the peripheral does not support low power states at all.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00195]\n⌈The\nAPI\nshall\nreport\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nPWM_E_-\nTRANSITION_NOT_POSSIBLE in case the requested power state cannot be directly\nreached from the current power state.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00196]\n⌈The\nAPI\nshall\nreport\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nPWM_E_-\nPERIPHERAL_NOT_PREPARED in case the HW unit has not been previously prepared\nfor the target power state by use of the API Pwm_PreparePowerState.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.5.1 Pwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager\n[SWS_Pwm_00189] Definition of scheduled function Pwm_Main_PowerTransi-\ntionManager ⌈\nService Name\nPwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager\nSyntax\nvoid Pwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager (\nvoid\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0d\nDescription\nThis API is cyclically called and supervises the power state transitions, checking for the\nreadiness of the module and issuing the callbacks IoHwAb_Pwm_NotifyReadyForPower\nState<Mode> (see PwmPowerStateReadyCbkRef configuration parameter).\nAvailable via\nSchM_Pwm.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00190] ⌈This API executes any non-immediate action needed to finalize\na power state transition requested by Pwm_PreparePowerState.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00191] ⌈The rate of scheduling shall be defined by Pwm MainSched-\nulePeriod and shall be variable, as the function only needs to be called if a transition\nhas been requested.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00192] ⌈This API shall also issue callback notifications to the eventually\nregistered users (IoHwAbs) as configured, only in case the asynch mode is chosen.⌋\n[SWS_Pwm_00193] ⌈In case the PWM module is not initialized, this function shall\nsimply return without any further elaboration. This is needed to avoid to elaborate\nuninitialized variables. No development error shall be entered, because this condition\ncan easily be verified during the startup phase (tasks started before the initialization is\ncomplete).\nRationale: during the startup phase it can happen that the OS already schedules tasks,\nwhich call main functions, while some modules are not initialised yet. This is no real\nerror condition, although need handling, i.e. returning without execution.\nAlthough the transition state monitoring functionality is mandatory, the implementation\nof this API is optional, meaning that if the HW allows for other ways to deliver notifica-\ntion and watch the transition state the implementation of this function can be skipped.⌋"
    },

module shall call the function Pwm_Notification_<#Channel> accordingly\nto the last call of Pwm_EnableNotification for channel <#Channel>.\nAvailable via\nPwm_Externals.h\n⌋()\n[SWS_Pwm_00025] ⌈The provide the functionality of\nPwm_EnableNotification only when the configuration parameter\nPwmNotificationSupported is ON. ⌋ ()\n[SWS_Pwm_20115] ⌈The Pwm module shall provide the functionality       "verbatim_text": "8.7.1 Optional Interfaces\nThis chapter defines all interfaces which are required to fulfill an optional functionality\nof the module.\n[SWS_EcuM_02859] Definition of optional interfaces requested by module EcuM\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00415, SRS_BSW_00477\n⌈\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nAdc_Init\nAdc.h\nInitializes the ADC hardware units and driver.\nCan_Init\nCan.h\nThis function initializes the module.\nCanTrcv_Init\nCanTrcv.h\nInitializes the CanTrcv module.\nDet_Init\nDet.h\nService to initialize the Default Error Tracer.\nDet_ReportError\nDet.h\nService to report development errors.\nEth_Init\nEth.h\nInitializes the Ethernet Driver\nEthSwt_Init\nEthSwt.h\nInitializes the Ethernet Switch Driver\nEthTrcv_Init\nEthTrcv.h\nInitializes the Ethernet Transceiver Driver\nFr_Init\nFr.h\nInitializes the Fr.\nFrTrcv_Init\nFrTrcv.h\nThis service initializes the FrTrcv.\nGetCoreID\nOs.h\nThe function returns a unique core identifier.\nGpt_Init\nGpt.h\nInitializes the GPT driver.\nIcu_Init\nIcu.h\nThis function initializes the driver.\nIoHwAb_Init<Init_Id>\nIoHwAb.h\nInitializes either all the IO Hardware Abstraction\nsoftware or is a part of the IO Hardware Abstraction.\nLin_Init\nLin.h\nInitializes the LIN module.\nLinTrcv_Init\nLinTrcv.h\nInitializes the Lin Transceiver Driver module.\nOcu_Init\nOcu.h\nService for OCU initialization.\nPort_Init\nPort.h\nInitializes the Port Driver module.\nPwm_Init\nPwm.h\nService for PWM initialization.\n▽\n△\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nShutdownAllCores\nOs.h\nAfter this service the OS on all AUTOSAR cores is\nshut down. Allowed at TASK level and ISR level and\nalso internally by the OS. The function will never\nreturn. The function will force other cores into a\nshutdown.\nSpi_Init\nSpi.h\nService for SPI initialization.\nStartCore\nOs.h\nIt is not supported to call this function after Start\nOS(). The function starts the core specified by the\nparameter CoreID. The OUT parameter allows the\ncaller to check whether the operation was\nsuccessful or not. If a core is started by means of\nthis function StartOS shall be called on the core.\nWdg_Init\nWdg.h\nInitializes the module.\nWdgM_PerformReset\nWdgM.h\nInstructs the Watchdog Manager to cause a\nwatchdog reset.\n⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.7 API parameter checking\n[SWS_Pwm_10051] ⌈If development error detection for the Pwm module is enabled,\nand a development error occurs, then the corresponding PWM function shall report\nthe error to the Default Error Tracer. ⌋ (SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386)\n[SWS_Pwm_20051] ⌈If development error detection for the Pwm module is enabled,\nand a development error occurs, then the corresponding PWM function shall skip the\ndesired functionality in order to avoid any corruptions of data or hardware registers\nleaving the function without any actions. ⌋ (SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386)\n[SWS_Pwm_00117] ⌈If development error detection for the Pwm module is enabled:\nif any function (except Pwm_Init) is called before Pwm_Init has been called, the\ncalled function shall raise development error PWM_E_UNINIT. ⌋ (SRS_BSW_00406,\nSRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386)\n[SWS_Pwm_00045]  ⌈If development error detection for the Pwm module is\nenabled: The API Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty() shall check if the given PWM\nchannel is of the channel class type PWM_VARIABLE_PERIOD. If this is not the case\nthe development error PWM_E_PERIOD_UNCHANGEABLE shall be called. ⌋\n(SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386)\n[SWS_Pwm_00047] ⌈If development error detection for the Pwm module is enabled:\nthe PWM functions shall check the parameter ChannelNumber and raise\ndevelopment error PWM_E_PARAM_CHANNEL if the parameter ChannelNumber is\ninvalid. ⌋ (SRS_BSW_00323, SRS_BSW_00386)"
    },

9.2: Asynchronous power state setting\nThe sequence diagram in figure 9.2 refers to a power state transition, where the periph-\nerals are configured for asynchronous power state transitions. Std_ReturnType Adc_SetupResultBuffer (Adc_GroupType Group, Adc_ValueGroupType* DataBufferPtr);

            
inicializa ADC controlador com o grupo específico resultado buffer iniciar endereço onde o conversão resultados será armazenado. o applicatio n tem para garantir que a aplicação buffer, onde dados buffer Ptr points para, pode hold todos o conversão resultados do especificado grupo. a inicialização com Adc_ Setup resultado buffer é exigido depois de reinicializado, antes de um grupo conversão pode ser iniciado.

Adc_StreamNumSampleType Adc_GetStreamLastPointer (Adc_GroupType Group, Adc_ValueGroupType* * PtrToSamplePtr);

            
devolve o número de válido amostras por canal, armazenado no resultado buffer. lê um ponteiro, pointing para um posição no grupo resultado buffer. com o ponteiro posição, o resultados de todos grupo canais do último concluído conversão round pode ser acc essed. com o ponteiro e o valor de retorno, todos válido grupo conversão resultados pode ser accessed (o utilizador tem para take o layout do resultado buffer em account).

<h4>Arquitetura do sistema &amp; papel do cluster de módulos</h4>
<p>O cluster “Microcontroller Abstraction” forma a camada de software mais baixa da Classic Platform. As especificações dos drivers ADC e PWM registram expressamente que esses módulos residem no nível de arquitetura mais baixo e, por isso, não oferecem callbacks para camadas inferiores (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications">SWS ADC p. 79</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications">SWS PWM p. 40</a>). Seus usuários são módulos da abstração de ECU e dos serviços de sistema, principalmente IoHwAb, WdgIf/WdgM, bem como EcuM e BswM. Normativos para a R20-11 são os Requirements do payload. Passagens de documentos de releases posteriores servem aqui apenas para fins ilustrativos, como o exemplo de ADC da IoHwAb (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/figures/FIG-a418e2fa072ee8a7.html" data-snip="FIG-a418e2fa072ee8a7">IoHwAb p. 55</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>O <strong>Adc</strong> converte canais analógicos em grupos. Uma conversão é disparada por software ou hardware (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00514" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00514">[SWS_Adc_00514]</a>). Os resultados ficam em buffers fornecidos pelo usuário (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_91000" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_91000">[SWS_Adc_91000]</a>).</li>
<li>O <strong>Pwm</strong> gera sinais modulados por largura de pulso com período e duty cycle (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_91001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_91001">[SWS_Pwm_91001]</a>). Opcionalmente, ele reporta bordas de sinal (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00109" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00109">[SWS_Pwm_00109]</a>).</li>
<li>O <strong>Wdg</strong> opera o watchdog de hardware interno ou externo por meio de uma condição de disparo (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00144" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00144">[SWS_Wdg_00144]</a>).</li>
<li>O <strong>Spi</strong> e o <strong>Dio</strong> estão comprovados no payload como vias de acesso de um watchdog externo (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00076" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00076">[SWS_Wdg_00076]</a>). O payload não contém Requirements de SWS próprios desses dois módulos.</li>
<li>O <strong>Port</strong> está comprovado via <code>Port_Init</code> como “Initializes the Port Driver module” na lista de interfaces do EcuM (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_OS_SECTION_8_7_1_Optional_Interfaces.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_OS_SECTION_8_7_1_Optional_Interfaces">SWS EcuM p. 142</a>). Um diagrama localiza a “Port Logic” entre a unidade PWM e o pino (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/figures/FIG-22f73e742491a849.html" data-snip="FIG-22f73e742491a849">RS PWM p. 14</a>).</li>
</ul>

<p class="diagram-note">Diagrama de contexto: Os drivers MCAL são inicializados por EcuM/BswM, utilizados por IoHwAb e WdgIf, e reportam erros ao DET/DEM; um watchdog externo acessa o hardware via Spi ou Dio. Fontes: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00076" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00076">[SWS_Wdg_00076]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00082" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00082">[SWS_Adc_00082]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00198" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00198">[SWS_Pwm_00198]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00111" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00111">[SWS_Wdg_00111]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00377" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00377">[SWS_Adc_00377]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00104" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00104">[SWS_Pwm_00104]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_4_1_Startup.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_4_1_Startup">Modemanagement p. 54</a></p>

<h4>Interação &amp; caminhos de interação</h4>
<p><strong>Caminho de dados do ADC.</strong> O fluxo começa com o buffer de resultados.</p>
<ol>
<li>Após cada reset e antes da primeira conversão de grupo, o usuário deve definir o buffer de resultados do grupo com <code>Adc_SetupResultBuffer</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_91000" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_91000">[SWS_Adc_91000]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_2_Adc_SetupResultBuffer.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_2_Adc_SetupResultBuffer">SWS ADC p. 54</a>).</li>
<li><code>Adc_StartGroupConversion</code> redefine o ponteiro interno do buffer. A notificação não é ativada automaticamente com isso (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00367" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00367">[SWS_Adc_00367]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_4_Adc_StartGroupConversion.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_4_Adc_StartGroupConversion">SWS ADC p. 57</a>).</li>
<li>Após cada conversão de grupo concluída, o driver chama <code>IoHwAb_AdcNotification&lt;#groupID&gt;</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00082" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00082">[SWS_Adc_00082]</a>).</li>
<li>O usuário lê os resultados por uma de duas vias:
<ul>
<li><code>Adc_ReadGroup</code> copia-os (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00369" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00369">[SWS_Adc_00369]</a>).</li>
<li><code>Adc_GetStreamLastPointer</code> fornece um ponteiro para o buffer (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00375" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00375">[SWS_Adc_00375]</a>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p>Quantos resultados o buffer comporta depende do modo de acesso: Single ou Streaming (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00528" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00528">[SWS_Adc_00528]</a>). No modo Streaming, o buffer é organizado de forma linear ou circular (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00519" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00519">[SWS_Adc_00519]</a>).</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Diagrama de sequência: Conversão contínua disparada por software com notificação – configurar buffer, ativar notificação, iniciar, notificar e ler a cada rodada, parar. Fontes: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_9_4_Software_triggered_continuous_conversion_with_notification.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_9_4_Software_triggered_continuous_conversion_with_notification">SWS ADC p. 92</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_91000" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_91000">[SWS_Adc_91000]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00082" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00082">[SWS_Adc_00082]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_11_Adc_GetGroupStatus.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_11_Adc_GetGroupStatus">SWS ADC p. 70</a></p>
<p><strong>Caminho de controle de PWM.</strong> O usuário ajusta o sinal por meio de dois serviços:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Pwm_SetDutyCycle</code> altera apenas o duty cycle (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_91000" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_91000">[SWS_Pwm_91000]</a>).</li>
<li><code>Pwm_SetPeriodAndDuty</code> altera o período e o duty cycle (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_91001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_91001">[SWS_Pwm_91001]</a>). O período só pode ser alterado em canais da classe <code>PWM_VARIABLE_PERIOD</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00110" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00110">[SWS_Pwm_00110]</a>); caso contrário, o driver reporta <code>PWM_E_PERIOD_UNCHANGEABLE</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_40002" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_40002">[SWS_Pwm_40002]</a>).</li>
</ul>
<p>Notificações de borda chegam ao usuário por meio de <code>Pwm_Notification_&lt;#Channel&gt;</code>. O determinante é a última chamada de <code>Pwm_EnableNotification</code> ou <code>Pwm_DisableNotification</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00105" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00105">[SWS_Pwm_00105]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_91004" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_91004">[SWS_Pwm_91004]</a>). <code>Pwm_GetOutputState</code> lê o estado interno do sinal de saída (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00100" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00100">[SWS_Pwm_00100]</a>). De acordo com o diagrama, essa é a tomada de sinal antes da lógica de porta, não o nível no pino (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/figures/FIG-22f73e742491a849.html" data-snip="FIG-22f73e742491a849">RS PWM p. 14</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Caminho do watchdog.</strong> A cadeia de chamadas percorre três níveis:</p>
<ul>
<li>O WdgM controla o driver por meio de <code>WdgIf_SetMode</code> e <code>WdgIf_SetTriggerCondition</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_OS_SECTION_8_6_1_Mandatory_interfaces_WATCHDOGMANAGER.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_OS_SECTION_8_6_1_Mandatory_interfaces_WATCHDOGMANAGER">SWS WdgM p. 86</a>).</li>
<li>O WdgIf mapeia esses serviços para a respectiva instância do driver por meio de <code>DeviceIndex</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_WDG_SECTION_8_3_Function_definitions_WATCHDOGINTERFACE.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_WDG_SECTION_8_3_Function_definitions_WATCHDOGINTERFACE">SWS WdgIf p. 17</a>).</li>
<li>O Wdg converte o timeout de milissegundos em um valor de contador, levando em consideração o modo atual (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00138" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00138">[SWS_Wdg_00138]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00139" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00139">[SWS_Wdg_00139]</a>).</li>
</ul>
<p>Watchdogs internos e externos diferem apenas no acesso ao hardware:</p>
<ul>
<li>Um driver interno acessa diretamente o hardware (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00161" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00161">[SWS_Wdg_00161]</a>).</li>
<li>Um driver externo utiliza Spi ou Dio e mantém os parâmetros necessários para isso em sua configuração (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00076" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00076">[SWS_Wdg_00076]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00078" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00078">[SWS_Wdg_00078]</a>).</li>
<li>As APIs de ambas as variantes são semanticamente idênticas (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00077" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00077">[SWS_Wdg_00077]</a>).</li>
<li>Se houver várias instâncias, os nomes das APIs são expandidos (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00172" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00172">[SWS_Wdg_00172]</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Sincronização, reentrância e contextos de tarefas</h4>
<p>Os módulos diferem claramente em suas garantias de reentrância:</p>
<ul>
<li>As APIs do caminho de dados do ADC são reentrantes.</li>
<li>Os serviços de PWM relacionados a canais são reentrantes apenas para canais distintos.</li>
<li>A inicialização, as APIs de power state e todos os serviços do Wdg não são reentrantes.</li>
</ul>
<table>
<thead><tr><th>API</th><th>Sync/Async</th><th>Reentrância</th><th>Referência</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>Adc_StartGroupConversion</code></td><td>assíncrono</td><td>reentrante</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00367" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00367">[SWS_Adc_00367]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>Adc_ReadGroup</code></td><td>síncrono</td><td>reentrante</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00369" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00369">[SWS_Adc_00369]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>Adc_SetPowerState</code></td><td>síncrono</td><td>não reentrante</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00475" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00475">[SWS_Adc_00475]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>Pwm_SetDutyCycle</code></td><td>assíncrono</td><td>reentrante para canais diferentes</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_91000" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_91000">[SWS_Pwm_91000]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>Pwm_Init</code></td><td>síncrono</td><td>não reentrante</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00095" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00095">[SWS_Pwm_00095]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>Wdg_SetMode</code> / <code>Wdg_SetTriggerCondition</code></td><td>síncrono</td><td>não reentrante</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00107" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00107">[SWS_Wdg_00107]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00155" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00155">[SWS_Wdg_00155]</a></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Para a consistência de dados, o Wdg define áreas exclusivas por meio do BSW Scheduler. Como módulo MCAL, o driver interno também pode desabilitar interrupções diretamente (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00040" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00040">[SWS_Wdg_00040]</a>). Durante a troca de modo e a rotina de operação, o estado <code>WDG_BUSY</code> indica acessos concorrentes (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00018" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00018">[SWS_Wdg_00018]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00052" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00052">[SWS_Wdg_00052]</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Funções agendadas.</strong> <code>Adc_Main_PowerTransitionManager</code> e <code>Pwm_Main_PowerTransitionManager</code> são executadas ciclicamente via SchM (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00479" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00479">[SWS_Adc_00479]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00189" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00189">[SWS_Pwm_00189]</a>). A sua taxa é variável, pois elas são necessárias apenas durante uma transição em andamento (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00500" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00500">[SWS_Adc_00500]</a>). Antes da inicialização, elas retornam sem notificação do DET (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00502" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00502">[SWS_Adc_00502]</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Contexto de interrupção.</strong> É provável que as notificações de grupo e de borda sejam executadas no contexto de interrupção. Dois fatores apontam para isso: o driver PWM redefine a flag de interrupção pertencente à notificação (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_6_3_Configurable_interfaces.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_6_3_Configurable_interfaces">SWS PWM p. 42</a>). Além disso, o exemplo do MemMap inclui uma <code>BswInterruptEntity</code> <code>Adc_IsrGroupScanCompleted</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_3_5_Allocatable_Memory_Parts.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_3_5_Allocatable_Memory_Parts">SWS MemMap p. 54</a>). Portanto, os callbacks devem permanecer curtos. A reentrância de <code>Pwm_Notification_&lt;#Channel&gt;</code> depende expressamente da implementação do usuário (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00105" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00105">[SWS_Pwm_00105]</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Sistemas multinúcleo.</strong> O Adc e o Pwm devem rejeitar mapeamentos de partições que a implementação não suporte (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00531" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00531">[SWS_Adc_00531]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00203" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00203">[SWS_Pwm_00203]</a>). As partições de kernel do ADC são um subconjunto das partições de usuário (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_CONSTR_00001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_CONSTR_00001">[SWS_Adc_CONSTR_00001]</a>). A isso se adequa o padrão Master-Satellite com divisão em kernel e parte de interface (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_2_2_7_Kernel_based_Master_Satellite_Realization.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_2_2_7_Kernel_based_Master_Satellite_Realization">BSW Distribution p. 18</a>).</p>

<h4>Ciclos de vida e modos operacionais</h4>
<p><strong>Inicialização.</strong> O EcuM chama <code>Adc_Init</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00365" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00365">[SWS_Adc_00365]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/figures/FIG-ad3d14a3906f0d48.html" data-snip="FIG-ad3d14a3906f0d48">SWS ADC p. 91</a>). A descrição da estrutura do EcuM menciona adicionalmente <code>Port_Init</code>, <code>Pwm_Init</code>, <code>Spi_Init</code> e <code>Wdg_Init</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_WDGM_SECTION_7_2_Structural_Description_of_the_ECU_Manager.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_WDGM_SECTION_7_2_Structural_Description_of_the_ECU_Manager">SWS EcuM p. 34</a>). Uma variante controlada pelo BswM inicializa na ordem Port, Dio, Adc, Spi (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_4_1_Startup.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_4_1_Startup">Modemanagement p. 54</a>). Interpretação: o Port provavelmente fica no início porque a configuração dos pinos é pré-requisito para os demais drivers de periféricos.</p>
<p><strong>ADC.</strong> O driver transiciona com <code>Adc_Init</code> de <code>ADC_UNINIT</code> para <code>ADC_INIT</code> e retorna com <code>Adc_DeInit</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_3_1_ADC_State_Diagram_for_One_Shot_Continuous_Group_Conversion_Mode.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_7_3_1_ADC_State_Diagram_for_One_Shot_Continuous_Group_Conversion_Mode">SWS ADC p. 31</a>). Cada grupo passa pelos estados <code>ADC_IDLE</code>, <code>ADC_BUSY</code>, <code>ADC_COMPLETED</code> e <code>ADC_STREAM_COMPLETED</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00513" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00513">[SWS_Adc_00513]</a>). O modo Continuous está disponível apenas com trigger de software (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00515" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00515">[SWS_Adc_00515]</a>). <code>Adc_DeInit</code> coloca o hardware em um estado semelhante a um reset (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00366" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00366">[SWS_Adc_00366]</a>). Ele só pode ser chamado quando todos os grupos estiverem em <code>ADC_IDLE</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_3_Adc_DeInit.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ADC_SECTION_8_3_3_Adc_DeInit">SWS ADC p. 59</a>).</p>
<p><strong>PWM.</strong> Após <code>Pwm_Init</code>, as saídas são Low, High ou moduladas, conforme a configuração. As notificações permanecem desativadas até que <code>Pwm_EnableNotification</code> seja chamado (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00095" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00095">[SWS_Pwm_00095]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/figures/FIG-42d2a53302c293d5.html" data-snip="FIG-42d2a53302c293d5">SWS PWM p. 46</a>). <code>Pwm_DeInit</code> define as saídas para o estado de Idle e desabilita as interrupções (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00096" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00096">[SWS_Pwm_00096]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_2_Pwm_DeInit.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_2_Pwm_DeInit">SWS PWM p. 27</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Watchdog.</strong> <code>Wdg_Init</code> define o modo padrão e o timeout inicial (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00001">[SWS_Wdg_00001]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00100" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00100">[SWS_Wdg_00100]</a>). Depois disso, os modos <code>WDGIF_OFF_MODE</code>, <code>WDGIF_SLOW_MODE</code> e <code>WDGIF_FAST_MODE</code> podem ser selecionados (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00160" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00160">[SWS_Wdg_00160]</a>). Não existe função de DeInit. A desativação é feita, se permitida, por meio do modo OFF (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Wdg_00031" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Wdg_00031">[SWS_Wdg_00031]</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Power states de Adc e Pwm.</strong> A transição ocorre em duas etapas:</p>
<ol>
<li><code>*_PreparePowerState</code> inicia-a (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00478" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00478">[SWS_Adc_00478]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00183" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00183">[SWS_Pwm_00183]</a>).</li>
<li>No caso assíncrono, a função principal conclui-a e reporta prontidão por meio de <code>IoHwAb_*_NotifyReadyForPowerState&lt;#Mode&gt;</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00480" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00480">[SWS_Adc_00480]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00198" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00198">[SWS_Pwm_00198]</a>).</li>
<li><code>*_SetPowerState</code> realiza a troca (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00475" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00475">[SWS_Adc_00475]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Pwm_00166" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Pwm_00166">[SWS_Pwm_00166]</a>).</li>
</ol>
<p>Previamente, os SWCs responsáveis, como a IoHwAb, devem definir os canais para Idle e cancelar o registro das notificações (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_9_Pwm_SetPowerState.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_PWM_SECTION_8_3_9_Pwm_SetPowerState">SWS PWM p. 36</a>). Na própria transição, são permitidas apenas reconfigurações específicas da transição (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Adc_00484" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Adc_00484">[SWS_Adc_00484]</a>).</p>
